Throughout the proof, epsilon_4 denotes a small positive number, whose value may change from one occurrence to the next, but ultimately is taken as an absolute constant. Fix bmL,j, and let Xi denote the empirical measure of configurations (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e) over all e=(av) such that bmL_a=bmL and j(v;a)=j. In the proof below we assume without loss of generality that the edge e has label SPINL_e=SPIN+. bemphStep 1. Reduction to entropy maximization for a conditional measure. Let SPINV denote the subset of all valid configurations (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e) that have Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2. Define the conditional measure \[ muBig(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus eBig) equiv Xibigg(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e\,bigg|\, SPINVbigg)\,. \] Note the marginals of mu must be close to those of the original measure Xi, since Lemma~ gives Xi(SPINV) ge bmvarpi_bmL,j(varsigma=SSPINwSSPINw) ge 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)\,. The measure mu maximizes entropy subject to the marginal distributions of sigma_e' for e'ne e, as well as of (Sigma_e)^i for i=1,2. By the method of Lagrange multipliers, we can express muBig(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus eBig) cong Bigg\prod_i=1,2 (b_e)^i((Sigma_e)^i)Bigg\ Bigg\ prod_e'in(delta v cup delta a)setminus e b_e'(sigma_e')Bigg\ 1_SPINV\,, where we fix (b_e)^i(SSPINw)equiv1 for both i=1,2. For xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, let us write (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)sim x if (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e) is consistent with frozen spin x_v=x. Note that for Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2, we have \[ bigg\smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e : (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)sim x bigg\ = S(x) equiv prod_i=1,2 S^i(x^i)\,, \] where S^i(x^i) bemphdoes not depend on Sigma_e. For instance, for all Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2, \[ bigg\smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e : (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e) sim SPIN+SPIN+ bigg\ =prod_i=1,2 overbraceBigg\(smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)^i : (smashvecsigma_delta v(SPIN-))^i equivSSPINy, (smashvecsigma_delta v(SPIN+)setminus e)^i equiv SSPINp, sum_e'in delta v(SPIN+)setminus e Ind(sigma_e')^i=SSPINrge1 Bigg\^S^i(SPIN+)\,. \] Consequently, the marginal of on (x_v,Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e) can be written as mu(x_v,Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e) =frac1_SPINVZ Bigg\prod_i=1,2 (b_e)^i((Sigma_e)^i)Bigg\ overbrace Bigg\sum_smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e in S(x_v) prod_e'indelta vsetminus e b_e'(sigma_e') Bigg\^textupdenote this b_v(x_v) Bigg\ prod_e'in delta asetminus e b_e'(sigma_e')Bigg\\,, where Z is the normalizing constant. We next turn to the construction and estimation of the weights in . bemphStep 2. Initialization of Lagrangian weights. We will construct weights b_tto b in the limit ttoinfty. At t=0, on the variable v and on the edges delta asetminus e, we put setlengthjot0pt2 nonumber b_v,0(x) &equiv mu_v(x) equiv mu(x_v=x) &&textupfor xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, \\ b_e',0(sigma) &equiv mu_e'(sigma) equiv mu( sigma_e'=sigma ) &&textupfor sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2 and e'indelta asetminus e. Abbreviate Kequiv k(bmL). On the central edge e=(av), for i=1,2 we put \[(b_e,0)^i( (Sigma_e)^i ) equiv frac(mu_e)^i( (Sigma_e)^i) 1/ (2^K)^Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SPINv \,. \] Let mu_t be defined as mu in , but with b_t in place of b, and normalizing constant Z_t. We begin by estimating the marginals at time t=0. Recalling the notation SSPINuequivsetSSPINy,SSPINc, we have \[ Z_0mu_e,0(SSPINwSSPINw) = (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e mu_e'(SSPINuSSPINu)Bigg\ Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\ = (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\\,, \] where the estimate uses and the assumption that bmL is nice, which implies (together with the judicious condition) Xi_e'(SSPINuSSPINu)ge 1-O(2^-k) for all e'indelta a. (In the above calculation, the O(k^2/2^k) error comes from the fact that among the configurations smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e with sigma_e'inSSPINuSSPINu for all e', some will not be compatible with sigma_e=SSPINwSSPINw because they will have too few SSPINc spins.) Next recall that (as noted in the proof of Lemma~) if bmL is both nice and diverse, then Lemma~ implies , which says that omega_bmL,j(SSPINySSPINb)ge1/65 for at least k/10 indices 1le jle k(bmL). Recall also that implies that the marginals of mu are close to those of the original measure Xi, so implies minBigg\ sum_j=1^k(bmL) 1bigg\ mu_j(SSPINySSPINb)gefrac166 bigg\, sum_j=1^k(bmL) 1bigg\ mu_j(SSPINbSSPINy)gefrac166 bigg\ Bigg\ ge frack10\,. It follows using that Z_0mu_e,0(SPINvSSPINw) &= (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) fracmu_v(SPIN+) 1/2 Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e fracmu_e'(SSPINySSPINu)1/2 Bigg\ Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg)Bigg\\\ &= (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg) Bigg\\,, where the factors of 1/2 come from the 2^K term in the definition of (b_e,0)^1(SPINv). Lastly, Z_0mu_e,0(SPINvSPINv) =overbrace frac(mu_e)^1(SPINv)1/2^K frac(mu_e)^2(SPINv)1/2^K ^O(1) overbracemu_v(SPIN+SPIN+) Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy) Bigg\^textupat most 2^-k(1+epsilon_4) by le Obigg( fracminset(mu_e)^1(SPINv),(mu_e)^2(SPINv) 2^kepsilon_4 bigg)\,. The above estimates imply that the single-copy marginals of mu_e,0 are close to those of mu_e: more precisely, we have bigg| frac(mu_e,0)^i(Sigma^i)(mu_e)^i(Sigma^i)-1 bigg| le k^O(1)/2^k &textupif Sigma^i=SSPINw,\\ O(2^-kepsilon_4) &textupif Sigma^i=SPINv,\\ for both i=1,2. We then turn to estimating the marginals at t=0 on the edges of delta asetminus e. For e'in delta asetminus e and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, we can represent the marginal probability of sigma on e' as mu_e',0(sigma) =sum_SigmainsetSSPINw,SSPINr^2 mu_e,0(Sigma) mu_0Big(sigma_e'=sigma\, Big|\,Sigma_e=SigmaBig)\,. The term mu_e,0(Sigma) was just estimated above, while the conditional probability mu_0(sigma_e'=sigma\,|\,Sigma_e=Sigma) can be obtained from the representation . Substituting these into gives mu_v,0(x) &stackrel= mu_e,0(SPINvSPINv)Indx=SPIN+SPIN+ + mu_e,0(SPINvSSPINw)fracmu_v(x) (mu_v)^1(SPIN+) Indx^1=SPIN+ + mu_e,0(SSPINwSPINv)fracmu_v(x) (mu_v)^2(SPIN+) Indx^2=SPIN+ +mu_e,0(SSPINwSSPINw) mu_v(x)\\ &stackrel= mu_v(x) Bigg\ Obigg(fracIndx=SPIN+SPIN+2^k(1+epsilon_4)bigg) +Obigg(fracIndx^1=SPIN+ + Indx^2=SPIN+2^kbigg) +1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg) Bigg\ =mu_v(x)Bigg\ 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg) Bigg\\,. To summarize the last few estimates, we have shown that at t=0 we have bigg\|fracmu_v,0mu_v-1bigg\|_infty + sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(mu_e,0)^i(SSPINw) (mu_e)^i(SSPINw)-1bigg| + sum_e'indelta asetminus v bigg\|fracmu_e',0mu_e'-1bigg\|_infty \\ sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(mu_e,0)^i(SPINv) (mu_e)^i(SPINv)-1bigg| le k^O(1) 2^-k\\ 2^-kepsilon_4 \,. We now turn to the construction of the sequence b_tto b_inftyequiv b, where we recall that b denotes the limiting weights in that give the solution to the constrained entropy maximization problem. bemphStep 3. Iterative construction and covariance estimates. For each tge0, suppose we have the weights b_t, which define the measure mu_t. We then define the weights at time t+1 by setting fracb_v,t+1(x)b_v,t(x) =fracmu_v(x)mu_v,t(x)\,, fracb_e',t+1(sigma)b_e',t(sigma) =fracmu_e'(sigma)mu_e',t(sigma) \,, frac(b_e,t+1)^i(Sigma^i)(b_e,t)^i(Sigma^i) =fracmu_e(Sigma^i)mu_e,t(Sigma^i) for all xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, e'indelta asetminus e, sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, i=1,2, and Sigma^iinsetSSPINw,SPINv. We will show by induction that for all tge0 we have the bound bigg\| fracmu_v,tmu_v -1bigg\|_infty +sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(mu_e,t)^i(SSPINw) (mu_e)^i(SSPINw)-1bigg| +sum_e'indelta asetminus e bigg\| fracmu_e',tmu_e'-1bigg\|_infty\\ sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(mu_e,t)^i(SPINv) (mu_e)^i(SPINv)-1bigg| le frack^O(1)(2^kepsilon_4)^t/2 2^-k\\2^-kepsilon_4 \,, where the base case t=0 follows from . Note that and together imply Bigg\ bigg\|fracb_v,t+1b_v,t-1bigg\|_infty +sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(b_e',t+1)^i(SSPINw) (b_e',t)^i(SSPINw) -1bigg| +sum_e'indelta asetminus e bigg\|fracb_e',t+1b_e',t-1bigg\|_infty Bigg\\\ sum_i=1,2 bigg|frac(b_e',t+1)^i(SPINv) (b_e',t)^i(SPINv) -1bigg| le frack^O(1)(2^kepsilon_4)^t/2 2^-k\\2^-kepsilon_4 \,, Towards the proof of , we estimate covariances under the measure mu_t. First, for all xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2 we have fracZ_t mu_t(x_v=x,(Sigma_e)^1=SSPINw) mu_v(x) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw) &=fracb_v,t(x) (b_e,t)^1(SSPINw)mu_v(x) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw) Bigg\ (b_e,t)^2(SSPINw) prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e',t(SSPINuSSPINu) bigg(1-frack^O(1)2^kbigg)\\ & +Indx^2=SPIN+(b_e,t)^2(SPINv) prod_e'b_e',t(SSPINuSSPINy) bigg(1-fracO(1)2^kepsilon_4bigg) Bigg\\\ &=fracb_v,t(x) (b_e,t)^1(SSPINw)mu_v(x) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw) Bigg\1-frack^O(1)2^kBigg\ stackrel= 1-frack^O(1)2^k\,. In combination with , this implies that for all xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2 and i=1,2 we have \[Bigg| fracCov_mu_t( Indx_v=x, Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SSPINw) mu_v(x) (mu_e)^i(SSPINw)Bigg| =Bigg| fracmu_t(x_v=x,(Sigma_e)^1=SSPINw) mu_v(x) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw) -fracmu_v,t(x) (mu_e,t)^1(SSPINw) mu_v(x) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw) Bigg| le frack^O(1)2^k\,. \] Next, for e'indelta asetminus e and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, we calculate fracZ_t mu_t((Sigma_e)^1=SSPINw, sigma_e'=sigma) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)mu_e'(sigma) &= frac(b_e,t)^1(SSPINw)b_e',t(sigma) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)mu_e'(sigma) Bigg\ (b_e,t)^2(SSPINw) prod_e''indelta asetminussete,e' b_e'',t(SSPINuSSPINu) bigg(1-frack^O(1)2^kbigg) \\ & +Indsigma^2=SSPINy (b_e,t)^2(SPINv) (b_v,t)^2(SPIN+) prod_e''indelta asetminussete,e' b_e'',t(SSPINuSSPINy) bigg(1-fracO(1)2^kepsilon_4bigg) Bigg\\\ &= frac(b_e,t)^1(SSPINw)b_e',t(sigma) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)mu_e'(sigma) Bigg\1- frack^O(1)2^kBigg\ stackrel= 1- frack^O(1)2^k\,. This implies that for all e'indelta asetminus e and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, we have \[ fracCov_mu_t( Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SSPINw, Indsigma_e'=sigma) (mu_e)^i(SSPINw) mu_e'(sigma) lefrack^O(1)2^k\,. \] Similar calculations for the case (Sigma_e)^i=SPINv give fracCov_mu_t(Indx_v=x, Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SPINv) mu_v(x) (mu_e)^i(SPINv) &le O(1)\,,\\ fracCov_mu_t( Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SPINv, Indsigma_e'=sigma) (mu_e)^i(SPINv) mu_e'(sigma) &le O(1)\,, for all xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, e'indelta asetminus e, and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2. Next, on the edge e=(av), we have \[ fracZ_tmu_e,t(SSPINwSSPINw) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) = frac(b_e,t)^1(SSPINw)(b_e,t)^2(SSPINw) (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e',t(SSPINuSSPINu) Bigg\1-frack^O(1)2^kBigg\ stackrel= 1- frack^O(1)2^k\,. \] Next, using the diversity bound , we also have fracZ_tmu_e,t(SPINvSSPINw) (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) &stackrel= frac(b_e,t)^1(SPINv)(b_e,t)^2(SSPINw) (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) (b_v,t)^1(SPIN+) prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e',t(SSPINySSPINu) Bigg\1-fracO(1)2^kepsilon_4Bigg\ \\ & stackrel= Bigg\1-fracO(1)2^kepsilon_4Bigg\ 2^K (b_v,t)^1(SPIN+) prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e',t(SSPINySSPINu) stackrel= 1-fracO(1)2^kepsilon_4\,,\\ fracZ_tmu_e,t(SPINvSPINv) (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SPINv) &= frac(b_e,t)^1(SPINv)(b_e,t)^2(SPINv) (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SPINv) mu_v(SPIN+SPIN+) prod_e'indelta vsetminus e b_e',t(SSPINySSPINy)\\ &stackrel= 2^K cdot 2^Kcdot mu_v(SPIN+SPIN+) prod_e'indelta vsetminus e b_e',t(SSPINySSPINy) stackrelle Obigg( frac2^k2^kepsilon_4bigg) \,. The last few estimates combined imply \[ fracCov_mu_t(Ind(Sigma_e)^1=Sigma^1, Ind(Sigma_e)^2=Sigma^2) (mu_e)^1(Sigma^1) (mu_e)^2(Sigma^2) le k^O(1) 2^-k&textupif Sigma=SSPINwSSPINw,\\ 2^-kepsilon_4&textupif SigmainsetSPINvSSPINw, SSPINwSPINv,\\ 2^k(1-epsilon_4) &textupif Sigma=SPINvSPINv. \] Lastly, it is straightforward to verify (details omitted) that \[fracCov_mu_t( Indx_v=x, Indsigma_e'=sigma) mu_v(x) mu_e'(sigma) le frack^O(1)2^k \] for all xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, e'indelta a setminus e, and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2. bemphStep 4. Estimates on Lagrangian weights. Now recall from that derivatives of mu_t-marginals with respect to b_t can be expressed as covariance. Let tildemu_t+1 be defined by \[ tildemu_t+1 Big(x_v,Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta asetminus eBig) = frac1tildeZ_t+1 b_v,t(x) (b_e,t+1)^1((Sigma_e)^1) (b_e,t)^2((Sigma_e)^2) prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e',t(sigma_e')\,, \] where tildeZ_t+1 is the normalizing constant. It follows from the update rule that the marginal of tildemu_t+1 on (Sigma_e)^1 is exactly the desired marginal (mu_e)^1. Consequently, delta_t+1(Sigma^1) &equiv bigg| frac(mu_e,t+1)^1(Sigma^1)(mu_e)^1(Sigma^1)-1 bigg| =bigg| frac(mu_e,t+1)^1(Sigma^1) (tildemu_e,t+1)^1(Sigma^1)-1bigg| \\ &le frac1(mu_e)^1(Sigma^1) OBigg( sum_x fracpartialmu_e,t+1(Sigma^1) partialln b_v,t+1(x) bigg| fracb_v,t+1(x)b_v,t(x)-1bigg| +sum_Sigma^2 fracpartialmu_e,t+1(Sigma^1) partialln (b_e,t+1)^2(Sigma^2) bigg| frac(b_e,t+1)^2(Sigma^2) (b_e,t)^2(Sigma^2) -1bigg| \\ & +sum_e',sigma fracpartialmu_e,t+1(Sigma^1) partialln b_e',t+1(sigma) bigg| fracb_e',t+1(sigma) b_e',t(sigma)-1bigg| Bigg)\,. Substituting the preceding covariance estimates into the last bound and applying gives delta_t+1(SSPINw) &le k^O(1)Bigg\ frac12^k cdot frac12^k(2^kepsilon_4/2)^t + frac12^kepsilon_4 cdot (mu_e)^2(SPINv) cdot bigg|frac(b_e,t+1)^2(SPINv) (b_e,t)^2(SPINv)-1 bigg| Bigg\\\ &le k^O(1)Bigg\ frac12^k cdot frac12^k(2^kepsilon_4/2)^t + frac12^kepsilon_4 cdot frac12^k cdot frac12^kepsilon_4((2^kepsilon_4/2)^t Bigg\ le frack^O(1)2^k(2^kepsilon_4/2)^t+2\,,\\ delta_t+1(SPINv) &le k^O(1)Bigg\ frac12^kepsilon_4((2^kepsilon_4/2)^t + 2^k(1-epsilon_4) cdot(mu_e)^2(SPINv) cdot frac12^kepsilon_4((2^kepsilon_4/2)^t Bigg\ le frack^O(1)2^kepsilon_4(2^kepsilon_4/2)^t+2\,. This verifies the inductive hypothesis for the quantities \[ delta_t+1(Sigma^i) = bigg|frac(mu_e,t+1)^i(Sigma^i) (mu_e)^i(Sigma^i)-1bigg|\,. \] The remaining estimates in follow by similar calculations (details omitted). It follows that as ttoinfty the weights b_t converge to the desired limiting weights b_inftyequiv b that define the optimal measure mu in . It then follows from the bound that mu_e(SPINvSPINv) &stackrel= OBigg( b_v(SPIN+SPIN+) Bigg\prod_i=1,2 (b_e)^i(SPINv)Bigg\ Bigg\ prod_e'indelta asetminus e b_e'(SSPINySSPINy)Bigg\ Bigg)\\ &stackrel= OBigg( mu_v(SPIN+SPIN+) prod_i=1,2Big( (mu_e)^i(SPINv) 2^KBig) prod_e'indelta asetminus e mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)Bigg) stackrelle frac12^k(1+epsilon_4)\,, as claimed.

nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, epsilon_4 denotes a small positive number, whose value may change from one occurrence to the next, but ultimately is taken as an absolute constant. Fix bmL,j, and let Xi denote the empirical measure of configurations (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e) over all e=(av) such that bmL_a=bmL and j(v;a)=j. In the proof below we assume without loss of generality that the edge e has label SPINL_e=SPIN+. bemphStep 1. Reduction to entropy maximization for a conditional measure. Let SPINV denote the subset of all valid configurations (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e) that have Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2. Define the conditional measure \[ muBig(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus eBig) equiv Xibigg(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus e\,bigg|\, SPINVbigg)\,. \] Note the marginals of mu must be close to those of the original measure Xi, since Lemma~ gives Xi(SPINV) ge bmvarpi_bmL,j(varsigma=SSPINwSSPINw) ge 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)\,. The measure mu maximizes entropy subject to the marginal distributions of sigma_e' for e'ne e, as well as of (Sigma_e)^i for i=1,2. By the method of Lagrange multipliers, we can express muBig(Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_(delta vcupdelta a)setminus eBig) cong Bigg\prod_i=1,2 (b_e)^i((Sigma_e)^i)Bigg\ Bigg\ prod_e'in(delta v cup delta a)setminus e b_e'(sigma_e')Bigg\ 1_SPINV\,, where we fix (b_e)^i(SSPINw)equiv1 for both i=1,2. For xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, let us write (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)sim x if (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e) is consistent with frozen spin x_v=x. Note that for Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2, we have \[ bigg\smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e : (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)sim x bigg\ = S(x) equiv prod_i=1,2 S^i(x^i)\,, \] where S^i(x^i) bemphdoes not depend on Sigma_e. For instance, for all Sigma_einsetSSPINw,SPINv^2, \[ bigg\smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e : (Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e) sim SPIN+SPIN+ bigg\ =prod_i=1,2 overbraceBigg\(smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e)^i : (smashvecsigma_delta v(SPIN-))^i equivSSPINy, (smashvecsigma_delta v(SPIN+)setminus e)^i equiv SSPINp, sum_e'in delta v(SPIN+)setminus e Ind(sigma_e')^i=SSPINrge1 Bigg\^S^i(SPIN+)\,. \] Consequently, the marginal of on (x_v,Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e) can be written as mu(x_v,Sigma_e,smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e) =frac1_SPINVZ Bigg\prod_i=1,2 (b_e)^i((Sigma_e)^i)Bigg\ overbrace Bigg\sum_smashvecsigma_delta vsetminus e in S(x_v) prod_e'indelta vsetminus e b_e'(sigma_e') Bigg\^textupdenote this b_v(x_v) Bigg\ prod_e'in delta asetminus e b_e'(sigma_e')Bigg\\,, where Z is the normalizing constant. We next turn to the construction and estimation of the weights in . bemphStep 2. Initialization of Lagrangian weights. We will construct weights b_tto b in the limit ttoinfty. At t=0, on the variable v and on the edges delta asetminus e, we put setlengthjot0pt2 nonumber b_v,0(x) &equiv mu_v(x) equiv mu(x_v=x) &&textupfor xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2, \\ b_e',0(sigma) &equiv mu_e'(sigma) equiv mu( sigma_e'=sigma ) &&textupfor sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2 and e'indelta asetminus e. Abbreviate Kequiv k(bmL). On the central edge e=(av), for i=1,2 we put \[(b_e,0)^i( (Sigma_e)^i ) equiv frac(mu_e)^i( (Sigma_e)^i) 1/ (2^K)^Ind(Sigma_e)^i=SPINv \,. \] Let mu_t be defined as mu in , but with b_t in place of b, and normalizing constant Z_t. We begin by estimating the marginals at time t=0. Recalling the notation SSPINuequivsetSSPINy,SSPINc, we have \[ Z_0mu_e,0(SSPINwSSPINw) = (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e mu_e'(SSPINuSSPINu)Bigg\ Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\ = (mu_e)^1(SSPINw)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\\,, \] where the estimate uses and the assumption that bmL is nice, which implies (together with the judicious condition) Xi_e'(SSPINuSSPINu)ge 1-O(2^-k) for all e'indelta a. (In the above calculation, the O(k^2/2^k) error comes from the fact that among the configurations smashvecsigma_delta asetminus e with sigma_e'inSSPINuSSPINu for all e', some will not be compatible with sigma_e=SSPINwSSPINw because they will have too few SSPINc spins.) Next recall that (as noted in the proof of Lemma~) if bmL is both nice and diverse, then Lemma~ implies , which says that omega_bmL,j(SSPINySSPINb)ge1/65 for at least k/10 indices 1le jle k(bmL). Recall also that implies that the marginals of mu are close to those of the original measure Xi, so implies minBigg\ sum_j=1^k(bmL) 1bigg\ mu_j(SSPINySSPINb)gefrac166 bigg\, sum_j=1^k(bmL) 1bigg\ mu_j(SSPINbSSPINy)gefrac166 bigg\ Bigg\ ge frack10\,. It follows using that Z_0mu_e,0(SPINvSSPINw) &= (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) fracmu_v(SPIN+) 1/2 Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e fracmu_e'(SSPINySSPINu)1/2 Bigg\ Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg)Bigg\\\ &= (mu_e)^1(SPINv)(mu_e)^2(SSPINw) Bigg\ 1 - Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg) Bigg\\,, where the factors of 1/2 come from the 2^K term in the definition of (b_e,0)^1(SPINv). Lastly, Z_0mu_e,0(SPINvSPINv) =overbrace frac(mu_e)^1(SPINv)1/2^K frac(mu_e)^2(SPINv)1/2^K ^O(1) overbracemu_v(SPIN+SPIN+) Bigg\prod_e'indelta asetminus e mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy) Bigg\^textupat most 2^-k(1+epsilon_4) by le Obigg( fracminset(mu_e)^1(SPINv),(mu_e)^2(SPINv) 2^kepsilon_4 bigg)\,. The above estimates imply that the single-copy marginals of mu_e,0 are close to those of mu_e: more precisely, we have bigg| frac(mu_e,0)^i(Sigma^i)(mu_e)^i(Sigma^i)-1 bigg| le k^O(1)/2^k &textupif Sigma^i=SSPINw,\\ O(2^-kepsilon_4) &textupif Sigma^i=SPINv,\\ for both i=1,2. We then turn to estimating the marginals at t=0 on the edges of delta asetminus e. For e'in delta asetminus e and sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, we can represent the marginal probability of sigma on e' as mu_e',0(sigma) =sum_SigmainsetSSPINw,SSPINr^2 mu_e,0(Sigma) mu_0Big(sigma_e'=sigma\, Big|\,Sigma_e=SigmaBig)\,. The term mu_e,0(Sigma) was just estimated above, while the conditional probability mu_0(sigma_e'=sigma\,|\,Sigma_e=Sigma) can be obtained from the representation . For instance, for each e'indelta asetminus e, we have \[ mu_0Big(sigma_e'=SSPINySSPINy\, Big|\,Sigma_e=SPINvSSPINwBig) stackrel= frac mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy) prod_e''indelta asetminussete,e' mu_e''(SSPINySSPINu) mu_e'(SSPINySSPINu) prod_e''indelta asetminussete,e' mu_e''(SSPINySSPINu) Bigg\1-Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg)Bigg\ = fracmu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)1/2 Bigg\1-Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg)Bigg\\,, \] where the last estimate uses that e' is a nice edge, so mu_e''(SSPINySSPINu) is close to 1/2. Similarly, \[mu_0Big(sigma_e'=SSPINySSPINy\, Big|\,Sigma_e=SSPINwSSPINwBig) stackrel= fracmu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)mu_e'(SSPINuSSPINu) Bigg\1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\ =mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy) Bigg\1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\\,. \] Lastly we have mu_0(sigma_e'=SSPINySSPINy\,|\,Sigma_e=SPINvSPINv)=1. Substituting the last few estimates into gives mu_e',0(SSPINySSPINy) &stackrel= mu_e,0(SPINvSPINv) +mu_e,0Big(setSPINvSSPINw,SSPINwSPINvBig) fracmu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)1/2 Bigg\1-Obigg(frac12^kepsilon_4bigg)Bigg\ +mu_e,0(SSPINwSSPINw) mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy) Bigg\1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\\\ &stackrel= mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)Bigg\ Obigg(frac12^k(1+epsilon_4)bigg) +Obigg( frac12^kbigg) + 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\ =mu_e'(SSPINySSPINy)Bigg\ 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg)Bigg\\,. By similar (but simpler) calculations, the same estimate holds for the other elements sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2. Lastly, we estimate the marginal law at t=0 for the frozen spin x_v, using a similar conditioning as in . To this end, note that \[ mu_0Big(x_v=x\,Big|\,Sigma_e=SSPINwSSPINwBig) stackrel= frac b_v,0(x) prod_i=1,2(b_e,0)^i(SSPINw) sum_x'insetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2 b_v,0(x') prod_i=1,2(b_e,0)^i(SSPINw) stackrel= mu_v(x) \] for any xinsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2. Likewise we have \[ mu_0Big(x_v=x\,Big|\,Sigma_e=SPINvSSPINwBig) stackrel= fracIndx^1=SPIN+ b_v,0(x) (b_e,0)^1(SPINv)(b_e,0)^2(SSPINw) sum_x'insetSPIN+ timessetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf b_v,0(x') (b_e,0)^1(SPINv)(b_e,0)^2(SSPINw) stackrel= fracmu_v(x)(mu_v)^1(SPIN+) Indx^1=SPIN+\,, \] and a similar expression holds for the case Sigma_e=SSPINwSSPINr. Lastly, note that mu_0(x_v=x\,Big|\,Sigma_e=SPINvSPINv) =Indx=SPIN+SPIN+. Substituting these into gives mu_v,0(x) &stackrel= mu_e,0(SPINvSPINv)Indx=SPIN+SPIN+ + mu_e,0(SPINvSSPINw)fracmu_v(x) (mu_v)^1(SPIN+) Indx^1=SPIN+ + mu_e,0(SSPINwSPINv)fracmu_v(x) (mu_v)^2(SPIN+) Indx^2=SPIN+ +mu_e,0(SSPINwSSPINw) mu_v(x)\\ &stackrel= mu_v(x) Bigg\ Obigg(fracIndx=SPIN+SPIN+2^k(1+epsilon_4)bigg) +Obigg(fracIndx^1=SPIN+ + Indx^2=SPIN+2^kbigg) +1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg) Bigg\ =mu_v(x)Bigg\ 1-Obigg(frack^22^kbigg) Bigg\\,. Then, for every edge eindelta v(SPIN+), we have (with epsilon_4 as in Lemma~) the bound \[ max_bmL,j bigg\omega_bmL,j(SSPINrSSPINr) : textupbmLinD with bmL(j)=bmt_e bigg\ le frac12^k(1+epsilon_4)\,. \] The same statement holds if we replace SPIN+ with SPIN- throughout. We claim that minBigg\ sum_ e indelta v(SPIN+) pi_eBig( setSSPINrSSPINr,SSPINrSSPINbBig), sum_ e indelta v(SPIN+) pi_eBig( setSSPINrSSPINr,SSPINbSSPINrBig) Bigg\ ge frack pi_v(SPIN+SPIN+)300\,. Let us first note that implies the result of the lemma: indeed, if holds, then condition of Lemma~ is satisfied with epsilon_2=1/300, and applying that lemma gives \[ omega_bmL,j(SSPINrSSPINr) le fracbmvarpi_bmL,j(upsilon=SPINvSPINv) 1- 2^-kepsilon_3 le OBig( bmvarpi_bmL,j (upsilon=SPINvSPINv)Big) \] for j=j(bmt) and all bmL such that bmL(j)=bmt. \label{c:RRFreq}
Consider the setting of Lemma~\ref{l:large11Case},
but without assuming a lower bound on $\pi_v(xx)$.
Then
	\[
	\sum_{e\in\delta v} 
	\sum_{\bm{L}\in\mathbb{D}}
	\pi_{\mathscr{D}}(\bm{L}\,|\,\bm{t}_e)
	\omega_{\bm{L},j(\bm{t}_e)} 
	(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r})
	\le \frac{k^2}{2^{k\epsilon_4}}
	\]
for $\epsilon_4$ as in Lemmas~\ref{l:ForcedRR}~and~\ref{l:large11Case}.

\begin{proof}
In view of Lemma~\ref{l:large11Case} it suffices to consider the case $\pi_v(\SPIN{+}\SPIN{+}) \le 2^{-k/16}$.
Suppose the conclusion of this corollary fails; more explicitly, suppose that
	\[
	\sum_{e\in\delta v} 
	\sum_{\bm{L}\in\mathbb{D}}
	\pi_{\mathscr{D}}(\bm{L}\,|\,\bm{t}_e)
	\omega_{\bm{L},j(\bm{t}_e)} 
	(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r})
	\ge \frac{k^4}{2^{k/16}}\,.
	\]
This implies that the assumption
\eqref{e:assumption.rr.avg} of Lemma~\ref{l:rrUnforced} holds, since
	\[
	\sum_{e\in\delta v} 
	\pi_e(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}\,|\, 
	\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{b}}^2)
	\ge \frac{k^4/2^{k/16}}{\pi_v(\SPIN{+}\SPIN{+})}
	\ge k^4\,.
	\]
In this case, combining 
Lemma~\ref{l:rrUnforced} and Lemma~\ref{l:ForcedRR} gives that for all $\bm{L},j$ with $\bm{L}(j)=\bm{t}_e$ for $e\in\delta v(\SPIN{+})$,
	\[
	\omega_{\bm{L},j}(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r})
	\le
	\frac{\omega_{\bm{L},j}(\SPIN{v}\SPIN{v})}{1-o_k(1)}
	\le
	\frac1{2^{k(1+\epsilon_4)}}\,,
	\]
from which the conclusion of this corollary follows.
\end{proof}

	\max
	\Bigg\{
	\Big|\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		-\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\Big|
	: \varsigma\in\set{
	\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{w},\SSPIN{y}\SSPIN{w},\SSPIN{c}\SSPIN{w},
	\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{c}}
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}\delta_{e,t}}{2^k}\,,\\
	\label{e:ZETA.delta.error.hat.iota.t}
	\max
	\Bigg\{
	\Big|\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		-\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\Big|
	: \varsigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c}}^2
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \hat{\iota} \delta_{e,t}\,, \\
	\label{e:ZETA.delta.error.mult.rr.t}
	\bigg|
		\frac{\bm{\zeta}_e(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}
		{\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	&\le\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}\,.
	\end{align}
At the initialization $t=0$ 
it follows from \eqref{e:ZETA.ww.unif.bound} and \eqref{e:ZETA.hat.iota.unif.bound} that
$\delta_{e,t} \le O(1)$
and $\ddot{\delta}_{e,t} \le O(2^{k(1-\epsilon)})$.
Denote
	\begin{equation}\label{e:ZETA.defn.delta.e.t}
	\bm{\delta}_t
	\equiv\sum_{e\in\delta v}\delta_{e,t}\,,\quad
	\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t
	\equiv\sum_{e\in\delta v}
		\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}\,.\quad
	\end{equation}
Let $t\ge0$ be an integer time, and suppose inductively that we have constructed the weights at time $t$. The marginal law on an edge $e\in\delta v$ is given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_t(\sigma_e=\sigma,\varsigma_e=\varsigma,\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong
	\Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\psi_{e,t}(\bm{L})
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2} (\beta_{e,t})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\,,
	\]
where $\dot{q}_{e,t}$ is the probability measure over $\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c}}^2$ defined by 
	\[
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\cong
	\sum_{\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v}:
		\sigma_e=\sigma}
	\psi_{v,t}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}})
	\prod_{e'\in\delta v\setminus e}
	\Bigg\{
	\sum_{\bm{L}_{e'}}
	\psi_{e',t}(\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
	\beta_{e',t}((\sigma_{e'})^i\,|\,\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg)
	\sum_{\varsigma_{e'}:
		\varsigma_{e'} \sim \sigma_{e'}}
	\chi_{e',t}(\varsigma_{e'}\,|\,\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg\}\,.
	\]
The conditional law of $(\sigma_e,\varsigma_e)$ given $\bm{L}_e$ is then given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_t(\sigma_e=\sigma,\varsigma_e=\varsigma\,|\,
		\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong \Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
		(\beta_{e,t})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\,.
	\]
For each $\bm{L}$, we apply Lemma~\ref{l:single.edge.sigma.varsigma} (below) to find updated weights $(\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})$ and $\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})$ such that, if we define $(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i
\equiv (\dot{\beta}_{e,t})^i \cdot (\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i$, then 
 the probability measure
	\[
	\tilde{\mu}_{e,t+3/4}
	(\sigma,\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	\cong
	\Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L}) 
	\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	\]
has $\varsigma$-marginal exactly $\bm{\zeta}_e(\cdot\,|\,\bm{L})$. The marginal law of $(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})$ at time $t+3/4$ is then given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_{t+3/4}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})
	\cong
	\psi_{v,t}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})
	\prod_{e\in\delta v}\Bigg\{
	\underbrace{
	\psi_{e,t}(\bm{L}_e)
	\sum_{\varsigma_e:\varsigma_e
		\sim \sigma_e}
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
		(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i((\sigma_e)^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
			\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma_e\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	}_{\cong \hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}(\sigma_e,\bm{L}_e)}
	\Bigg\}\,,
	\]
where $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ is a probability measure over pairs $(\sigma,\bm{L})$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:single.edge.sigma.varsigma} that
	\begin{equation}\label{e:ZETA.hq.first.error}
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t},\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4})
	\le
	\max_{\bm{L}}\left\{
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\hat{\iota}_{e,\bm{L}}&0\\
	2^k \hat{\iota}_{e,\bm{L}}&0\\
	1&1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\delta_{e,t}\\
	\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}
	\end{pmatrix}
	\right\}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:ZETA.hat.iota.unif.bound}}{\le}
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k(1+\epsilon)}&0\\
	2^{-k\epsilon}&0\\
	1&1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\delta_{e,t}\\
	\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}
	\end{pmatrix}
	\,.\end{equation}
Then apply Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} (where the $\hat{p}_e$ and $\hat{q}_e$ of 
Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} are given by
$\hat{q}_{e,t}$ and $\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}$ respectively) to find new weights $\psi_{v,t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}})$, $\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L})$, and $(\dot{\beta}_{e,t+1})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})$ such that, if we define
$(\beta_{e,t+1})^i \equiv (\dot{\beta}_{e,t+1})^i(\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i$,
then the probability measure
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_{t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\varsigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})
	\cong
	\psi_{v,t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})
	\prod_{e\in\delta v}\Bigg\{
	\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg(
	\prod_{i=1,2}
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^i((\sigma_e)^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg)
		\chi_{e,t+1}(\varsigma_e\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg\}\,,
	\]
has a marginal on $(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\bm{L}_{\delta v})$ that is fully judicious
(in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:judicious.augmented.alphabet}). In the notation of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate}, in going between $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ and $\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}$ we have
	\[
	\textup{\textsf{err}}_v
	= \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}
	= \sum_{e\in\delta v}
	\frac{\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}}
		{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
	= \frac{\bm{\delta}_t + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}\,,
	\]
using the notation of \eqref{e:ZETA.defn.delta.e.t}.
It then follows from the bound \eqref{e:ctypes.varupdate.MAINBOUND} of 
Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} that
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	\max_{\bm{L}}\Bigg\{
	\bigg|\frac{\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L})}{\psi_{e,t+3/4}(\bm{L})}
	-1\bigg|
	+ \max_{\tau\ne\SSPIN{r}}
	\bigg|\frac{(\beta_{e,t+1})^i(\tau\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\tau\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
		\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
	\,,\\
	\max_{\bm{L}}\Bigg\{
	\bigg|\frac{(\beta_{e,t+1})^i(\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
		\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
			\,.
	\label{e:ZETA.beta.last.error}
	\end{align}
It follows from the bound \eqref{e:ctypes.varupdate.OUTMSG} of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} that
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	\dddot{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\dot{q}_{e,t},\dot{q}_{e,t+1})
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\
	2^{-k\epsilon}
	\end{pmatrix}
		\textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}
	+k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	0&0&0\\
	0&1&1\\
	0&1&1\\
	1&2^{-k}&2^{-k}\\
	1&1&1\\
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k(1+\epsilon)}\delta_{e,t}\\
	2^{-k\epsilon}\delta_{e,t}\\
	2^{-k\epsilon} \min\set{ \delta_{e,t}
		+ \ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1} 
	\end{pmatrix} \\
	&\le
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\
	2^{-k\epsilon}
	\end{pmatrix} 
	\frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t
		}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
	+k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	0\\1\\1\\ 0\\1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{\delta_{e,t}
		+\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}}
		{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\label{e:ZETA.qdot.error}
	\end{align}
At time $t+1$ we have
	\[
	\frac{\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
		{\bm{\zeta}_{e,t+1}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
	=
	\frac{\displaystyle
	z_{e,t+1}\sum_{\sigma:\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^1(\sigma^1)
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^2(\sigma^2)
	 \chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{\displaystyle
	\tilde{z}_{e,t+3/4}
	\sum_{\sigma:\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t+1}(\sigma)
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^1(\sigma^1)
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^2(\sigma^2)
	 \chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	}
	\]
for normalizing constants $\tilde{z}_{e,t+3/4}$ and $z_{e,t+1}$. Combining with \eqref{e:ZETA.beta.last.error} and \eqref{e:ZETA.qdot.error} then gives
	\[
	\delta_{e,t+1}
	+\ddot{\delta}_{e,t+1}
	\le
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg(
	\frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^k}
	+ \delta_{e,t} 
	+ \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
	\Bigg)\,.
	\]
This concludes our analysis of the update procedure.\smallskip

\noindent\bemph{Part~5. Conclusion.}
Summing the preceding bound over all $e\in\delta v$ gives
	\begin{align*}
	\sum_{t\ge0} (\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t)
	&\le \bm{\delta}_0 + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_0
	+ 
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\sum_{t\ge0} (\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t)
	\le O(\bm{\delta}_0 + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_0)
	\le O(k 2^k)\,,\\
	\sum_{t\ge0} 
	(\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1})
	&\le 
	\delta_{e,0} + \ddot{\delta}_{e,0}
		+ \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
		 \sum_{t\ge0}
		\Bigg( \frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^k}+
		\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
		\Bigg)
	\le O(1)\,.
	\end{align*}
We can use the above bounds with \eqref{e:ZETA.beta.last.error} to obtain
	\[
	\sum_{t\ge0} \widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4},\hat{q}_{e,t+1})
	\le \begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k} \\ 1 \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\sum_{t\ge0}
	\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
	\le \begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k} \\ 1 \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{k^{O(1)} }{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\]	
Combining with \eqref{e:ZETA.hq.first.error} gives
	\[
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,0},\hat{q}_{e,\infty})
	\le O(1)
	\sum_{t\ge0}\Bigg\{
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t},\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4})
	+\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4},\hat{q}_{e,t+1})
	\Bigg\}
	\le
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k}\\
	1\\
	2^k 
	\end{pmatrix}\,.
	\]
(We also see that 
condition~\eqref{e:condition.on.hat.msg.with.L}
is satisfied by $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ for all $t\ge0$, so that 
the above applications of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} are justified.)
We also obtain from \eqref{e:ZETA.qdot.error} that
	\[
	\dddot{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\dot{q}_{e,0},\dot{q}_{e,\infty})
	\le
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix} 
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\]
The above estimates imply that for all $\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}^2\setminus\set{\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}}$ we have
	\[\mathbf{P}(\sigma_e=\sigma\,|\,\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong \dot{q}_{e,\infty}(\sigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		\hat{q}_{e,\infty}(\sigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	= {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}_e(\sigma) {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\hat{q}_e(\sigma)
		\Bigg( 1 + \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg)
	= {}_{*}\omega_e(\sigma)
		\Bigg( 1 + \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg)\,.
	\]
This implies the claimed bounds \eqref{e:balanceMarg}.
\end{proof}

\noindent\bemph{Part~2. Single-copy weights.} We first consider the simpler problem of setting weights in the single-copy model. For this discussion, let $\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}$ and $\varsigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c},\SSPIN{w}}$, and again write $\sigma\sim\varsigma$ to indicate compatibility.
Given a probability measure ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi$ over $\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}$, along with a probability measure ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta$ over spins $\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c},\SSPIN{w}}$ such that ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{r})={}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{r})$, we look for weights ${}_\star b$ and ${}_\star x$ such that
	\begin{equation}\label{e:mu.single.edge.sigma.varsigma}
	\mu(\sigma,\varsigma)
	\equiv
	\Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\sigma)
	{}_\star b(\sigma)
	{}_\star x(\varsigma)
	\end{equation}
defines a probability measure over $(\sigma,\varsigma)$ whose marginal on $\sigma$ is ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi$, and whose marginal on $\varsigma$ is ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta$. Explicitly, for the $\sigma$-marginal to be ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi$ we must have the equations
	{\setlength{\jot}{0pt}\begin{align*}
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{r}) &= {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{r}) {}_\star b(\SSPIN{r}){}_\star x(\SSPIN{r})
		= {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{r})\,,\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y}) &= {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{y}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{y})[{}_\star x(\SSPIN{y})
		+{}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})]\,,\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{g}) &={}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{g}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{g})[{}_\star x(\SSPIN{c})
		+{}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})]\,,\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{b}) &={}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{b}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{b})[{}_\star x(\SSPIN{c})
		+{}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})]\,.\end{align*}
For the $\varsigma$-marginal to be ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta$ we must have the equations
	\begin{align*}{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})
		&={}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{y}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{y}){}_\star x(\SSPIN{y})\,,\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})
		&=[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{g}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{g}) 
			+{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{b}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{b}) ]
			{}_\star x(\SSPIN{c})\,,\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{w})
		&=[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{y}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{y})
		+{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{g}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{g})
	+{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{b}){}_\star b(\SSPIN{b})
	]{}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})\,.
	\end{align*}}
Note also that if we multiply all the ${}_\star b$-weights by a scaling factor and divide all the ${}_\star x$-weights by the same factor, it has no effect on the right-hand side of \eqref{e:mu.single.edge.sigma.varsigma}, so without loss we can pin down the weights by requiring
${}_\star b(\SSPIN{r})=1$ and ${}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})=1$.
Then, combining the equations for ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y})$ and ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})$ gives
	\[
	{}_\star b(\SSPIN{y}) =\frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{y})}\,,\quad
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{y}) = \frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})}\,.
	\]
Next, comparing the equations for ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{g})$ and ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{b})$ gives
	\[
	\frac{{}_\star b(\SSPIN{g})}{{}_\star b(\SSPIN{b})}
	= \frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{g})/{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{g})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{b})/{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{b})}
	= \frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\hat{q}(\SSPIN{g})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\hat{q}(\SSPIN{b})}=1\,,
	\]
and we hereafter denote ${}_\star b(\SSPIN{c})\equiv {}_\star b(\SSPIN{g})\equiv{}_\star b(\SSPIN{b})$. 
Combining with the equations for 
${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{g})$, ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{b})$, and ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})$ gives
	\[
	{}_\star b(\SSPIN{c})=
	\frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{g})+{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{b})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})}
		{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{g}) + {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{b})}
	= \frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{c})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{c})}\,,\quad
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{c})
	=\frac{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})}{{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{c})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})}\,.
	\]
In summary, a valid solution is given by taking
	\begin{align}\label{e:ZETA.bstar}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	{}_\star b(\SSPIN{r})\\
	{}_\star b(\SSPIN{y})\\
	{}_\star b(\SSPIN{g})={}_\star b(\SSPIN{b})
	\equiv{}_\star b(\SSPIN{c})
	\end{pmatrix}
	&= 
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\
	[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})]/{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{y})\\
	[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{c})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})]/{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{c})
	\end{pmatrix}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:ZETA.zetastar}}{=} 
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\Theta(1)\\ \Theta(1) \\ \Theta(1)
	\end{pmatrix}\,,\\
	\label{e:ZETA.xstar}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{r})\\
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{y})\\
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{c})\\
	{}_\star x(\SSPIN{w})
	\end{pmatrix}
	&=\begin{pmatrix}
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{r})/{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}(\SSPIN{r})\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})/[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{y})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{y})]\\
	{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})/[{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi(\SSPIN{c})-{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta(\SSPIN{c})]\\
	1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:ZETA.zetastar}}{=} 
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\Theta(1/2^k)\\
	\Theta(k/2^k)\\
	\Theta(k/2^k)\\ 1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\,.\end{align}
Substituting these into \eqref{e:mu.single.edge.sigma.varsigma}
gives a measure with the desired marginals ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi$ and ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta$.\smallskip



\noindent\bemph{Part~3. Initialization in pair model.} Returning to \eqref{e:final.D.L.Lagrangian.form}, our goal is to construct a sequence of measures
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_t(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},
	\smash{\vec{\varsigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})
	\cong
	\psi_{v,t}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})
	\prod_{e\in\delta v}\Bigg\{
	\psi_{e,t}(\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg(
	\prod_{i=1,2}
	(\beta_{e,t})^i((\sigma_e)^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg)
		\chi_{e,t}(\varsigma_e\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg\}\]
which converges as $t\to\infty$ to the desired solution $\mathbf{P}_\infty\equiv\mathbf{P}$. We will further decompose the $\beta$ weights as
	\[
	(\beta_{e,t})^i( \sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\equiv
	\bigg\{(\dot{\beta}_{e,t})^i( \sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)\bigg\}
	\cdot
	\bigg\{(\hat{\beta}_{e,t})^i( \sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)\bigg\}
	\]
such that $(\hat{\beta}_{e,t})^i$ does not distinguish between $\SSPIN{g}$ and $\SSPIN{b}$, that is, such that
	\[
	(\hat{\beta}_{e,t})^i( \SSPIN{g}\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	=(\hat{\beta}_{e,t})^i( \SSPIN{b}\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\equiv(\hat{\beta}_{e,t})^i( \SSPIN{c}\,|\,\bm{L}_e)\,.
	\]
This is clearly an over-parametrization, so the $\dot{\beta}$ and $\hat{\beta}$ weights will not be uniquely determined; we need only find one choice of weights such that the resulting measure \eqref{e:final.D.L.Lagrangian.form} satisfies the constraints \eqref{e:final.D.L.clause}--\eqref{e:final.D.L.varsigma}. The overparametrization will be useful below because it allows for some separation between the analysis of the $\varsigma$-marginals and the analysis of the $(\sigma,\bm{L})$-marginals.

We initialize the construction at $t=0$ as follows.
We first set $\psi_{v,0}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})$ to be equal to $\varphi_v(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})$, which we recall from
\eqref{e:color.factor.model} is simply
the indicator of a valid pair coloring $\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v}$.
For an edge $e$ of type $\bm{t}$, let ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi_e\equiv{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\pi_{\bm{t}}$ be the canonical marginal on $\sigma^i$, and let ${}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta_e\equiv{}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta_{\bm{t}}$ be the canonical marginal on $\varsigma^i$, as discussed above.
Let ${}_\star b_e$ and ${}_\star x_e$ be the corresponding weights defined by \eqref{e:ZETA.bstar} and \eqref{e:ZETA.xstar}; in particular, we recall
from \eqref{e:ZETA.bstar} that ${}_\star b_e$
does not distinguish between $\SSPIN{g}$ and $\SSPIN{b}$. We then set
	{\setlength{\jot}{0pt}\begin{alignat*}{2}
	\psi_{e,0}(\bm{L})
		&\equiv\pi_{\mathscr{D}}(\bm{L}\,|\,\bm{t}_e)
		\quad
		&&\textup{for all $\bm{L}$,}\\
	(\dot{\beta}_{e,0})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})
		&\equiv 1
		&&\textup{for
		$i=1,2$,
		all $\bm{L}$,
		and all $\sigma^i\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}$,}\\
	(\hat{\beta}_{e,0})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})
		&\equiv {}_\star b_e(\sigma^i)\quad
		&&\textup{for
		$i=1,2$,
		all $\bm{L}$,
		and all $\sigma^i\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}$,}\\
	\chi_{e,0}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		&\equiv 
		{}_\star x_e(\varsigma^1)
		{}_\star x_e(\varsigma^2)\quad
		&&\textup{for all 
		$\bm{L}$ and all $\varsigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c},\SSPIN{w}}^2$.}
	\end{alignat*}}
Thus at $t=0$ the measure $\mathbf{P}_0$ will satisfy constraints 
\eqref{e:final.D.L.clause} and \eqref{e:final.D.L.judicious}, but not
\eqref{e:final.D.L.varsigma}, since we will have
	\[
	\bm{\zeta}_{e,0}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	\equiv
	\mathbf{P}_0(\varsigma_e=\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	=\prod_{i=1,2} {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\zeta_e(\varsigma^i)\,,
	\]
which in general is not the same as
$\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})$.\smallskip

\noindent\bemph{Part~4. Update procedure.}
In this step we will make use of Lemma~\ref{l:single.edge.sigma.varsigma}, which is stated and proved below. For $t\ge0$ let $\delta_{e,t}$ and $\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}$ denote parameters such that the estimates \eqref{e:ZETA.delta.error}--\eqref{e:ZETA.delta.error.mult.rr} below hold for the error between $\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\cdot\,|\,\bm{L})$ versus $\bm{\zeta}_e(\cdot\,|\,\bm{L})$ --- that is to say,
for all clause types $\bm{L}$ that can appear incident to edge $e$, we assume that
	\begin{align}
	\label{e:ZETA.delta.error.t}
	\max
	\Bigg\{
	\Big|\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		-\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\Big|
	: \varsigma\in\set{
	\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{w},\SSPIN{y}\SSPIN{w},\SSPIN{c}\SSPIN{w},
	\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{w}\SSPIN{c}}
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}\delta_{e,t}}{2^k}\,,\\
	\label{e:ZETA.delta.error.hat.iota.t}
	\max
	\Bigg\{
	\Big|\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		-\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\Big|
	: \varsigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c}}^2
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \hat{\iota} \delta_{e,t}\,, \\
	\label{e:ZETA.delta.error.mult.rr.t}
	\bigg|
		\frac{\bm{\zeta}_e(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}
		{\bm{\zeta}_{e,t}(\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	&\le\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}\,.
	\end{align}
At the initialization $t=0$ 
it follows from \eqref{e:ZETA.ww.unif.bound} and \eqref{e:ZETA.hat.iota.unif.bound} that
$\delta_{e,t} \le O(1)$
and $\ddot{\delta}_{e,t} \le O(2^{k(1-\epsilon)})$.
Denote
	\begin{equation}\label{e:ZETA.defn.delta.e.t}
	\bm{\delta}_t
	\equiv\sum_{e\in\delta v}\delta_{e,t}\,,\quad
	\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t
	\equiv\sum_{e\in\delta v}
		\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}\,.\quad
	\end{equation}
Let $t\ge0$ be an integer time, and suppose inductively that we have constructed the weights at time $t$. The marginal law on an edge $e\in\delta v$ is given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_t(\sigma_e=\sigma,\varsigma_e=\varsigma,\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong
	\Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\psi_{e,t}(\bm{L})
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2} (\beta_{e,t})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\,,
	\]
where $\dot{q}_{e,t}$ is the probability measure over $\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{c}}^2$ defined by 
	\[
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\cong
	\sum_{\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v}:
		\sigma_e=\sigma}
	\psi_{v,t}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}})
	\prod_{e'\in\delta v\setminus e}
	\Bigg\{
	\sum_{\bm{L}_{e'}}
	\psi_{e',t}(\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
	\beta_{e',t}((\sigma_{e'})^i\,|\,\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg)
	\sum_{\varsigma_{e'}:
		\varsigma_{e'} \sim \sigma_{e'}}
	\chi_{e',t}(\varsigma_{e'}\,|\,\bm{L}_{e'})
	\Bigg\}\,.
	\]
The conditional law of $(\sigma_e,\varsigma_e)$ given $\bm{L}_e$ is then given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_t(\sigma_e=\sigma,\varsigma_e=\varsigma\,|\,
		\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong \Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
		(\beta_{e,t})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})\,.
	\]
For each $\bm{L}$, we apply Lemma~\ref{l:single.edge.sigma.varsigma} (below) to find updated weights $(\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})$ and $\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})$ such that, if we define $(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i
\equiv (\dot{\beta}_{e,t})^i \cdot (\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i$, then 
 the probability measure
	\[
	\tilde{\mu}_{e,t+3/4}
	(\sigma,\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	\cong
	\Ind{\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L}) 
	\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	\]
has $\varsigma$-marginal exactly $\bm{\zeta}_e(\cdot\,|\,\bm{L})$. The marginal law of $(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})$ at time $t+3/4$ is then given by
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_{t+3/4}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})
	\cong
	\psi_{v,t}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})
	\prod_{e\in\delta v}\Bigg\{
	\underbrace{
	\psi_{e,t}(\bm{L}_e)
	\sum_{\varsigma_e:\varsigma_e
		\sim \sigma_e}
	\Bigg(\prod_{i=1,2}
		(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i((\sigma_e)^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
			\Bigg)
	\chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma_e\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	}_{\cong \hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}(\sigma_e,\bm{L}_e)}
	\Bigg\}\,,
	\]
where $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ is a probability measure over pairs $(\sigma,\bm{L})$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:single.edge.sigma.varsigma} that
	\begin{equation}\label{e:ZETA.hq.first.error}
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t},\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4})
	\le
	\max_{\bm{L}}\left\{
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\hat{\iota}_{e,\bm{L}}&0\\
	2^k \hat{\iota}_{e,\bm{L}}&0\\
	1&1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\delta_{e,t}\\
	\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}
	\end{pmatrix}
	\right\}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:ZETA.hat.iota.unif.bound}}{\le}
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k(1+\epsilon)}&0\\
	2^{-k\epsilon}&0\\
	1&1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	\delta_{e,t}\\
	\ddot{\delta}_{e,t}
	\end{pmatrix}
	\,.\end{equation}
Then apply Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} (where the $\hat{p}_e$ and $\hat{q}_e$ of 
Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} are given by
$\hat{q}_{e,t}$ and $\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}$ respectively) to find new weights $\psi_{v,t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}})$, $\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L})$, and $(\dot{\beta}_{e,t+1})^i(\sigma^i\,|\,\bm{L})$ such that, if we define
$(\beta_{e,t+1})^i \equiv (\dot{\beta}_{e,t+1})^i(\hat{\beta}_{e,t+3/4})^i$,
then the probability measure
	\[
	\mathbf{P}_{t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\varsigma}}_{\delta v},\smash{\vec{\bm{L}}}_{\delta v})
	\cong
	\psi_{v,t+1}(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v})
	\prod_{e\in\delta v}\Bigg\{
	\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg(
	\prod_{i=1,2}
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^i((\sigma_e)^i\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg)
		\chi_{e,t+1}(\varsigma_e\,|\,\bm{L}_e)
	\Bigg\}\,,
	\]
has a marginal on $(\smash{\vec{\sigma}}_{\delta v},\bm{L}_{\delta v})$ that is fully judicious
(in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:judicious.augmented.alphabet}). In the notation of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate}, in going between $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ and $\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4}$ we have
	\[
	\textup{\textsf{err}}_v
	= \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}
	= \sum_{e\in\delta v}
	\frac{\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}}
		{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
	= \frac{\bm{\delta}_t + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}\,,
	\]
using the notation of \eqref{e:ZETA.defn.delta.e.t}.
It then follows from the bound \eqref{e:ctypes.varupdate.MAINBOUND} of 
Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} that
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	\max_{\bm{L}}\Bigg\{
	\bigg|\frac{\psi_{e,t+1}(\bm{L})}{\psi_{e,t+3/4}(\bm{L})}
	-1\bigg|
	+ \max_{\tau\ne\SSPIN{r}}
	\bigg|\frac{(\beta_{e,t+1})^i(\tau\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\tau\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
		\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
	\,,\\
	\max_{\bm{L}}\Bigg\{
	\bigg|\frac{(\beta_{e,t+1})^i(\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^i(\SSPIN{r}\,|\,\bm{L})}-1\bigg|
	\Bigg\}
	&\le \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
		\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
			\,.
	\label{e:ZETA.beta.last.error}
	\end{align}
It follows from the bound \eqref{e:ctypes.varupdate.OUTMSG} of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} that
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	\dddot{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\dot{q}_{e,t},\dot{q}_{e,t+1})
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\
	2^{-k\epsilon}
	\end{pmatrix}
		\textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}
	+k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	0&0&0\\
	0&1&1\\
	0&1&1\\
	1&2^{-k}&2^{-k}\\
	1&1&1\\
	\end{pmatrix}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k(1+\epsilon)}\delta_{e,t}\\
	2^{-k\epsilon}\delta_{e,t}\\
	2^{-k\epsilon} \min\set{ \delta_{e,t}
		+ \ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1} 
	\end{pmatrix} \\
	&\le
	k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\
	2^{-k\epsilon}
	\end{pmatrix} 
	\frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t
		}{2^{k(1+\epsilon)}}
	+k^{O(1)}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	0\\1\\1\\ 0\\1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{\delta_{e,t}
		+\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}}
		{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\label{e:ZETA.qdot.error}
	\end{align}
At time $t+1$ we have
	\[
	\frac{\bm{\zeta}_e(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
		{\bm{\zeta}_{e,t+1}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
	=
	\frac{\displaystyle
	z_{e,t+1}\sum_{\sigma:\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t}(\sigma)
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^1(\sigma^1)
	(\beta_{e,t+3/4})^2(\sigma^2)
	 \chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})}
	{\displaystyle
	\tilde{z}_{e,t+3/4}
	\sum_{\sigma:\sigma\sim\varsigma}
	\dot{q}_{e,t+1}(\sigma)
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^1(\sigma^1)
	(\beta_{e,t+1})^2(\sigma^2)
	 \chi_{e,t+3/4}(\varsigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	}
	\]
for normalizing constants $\tilde{z}_{e,t+3/4}$ and $z_{e,t+1}$. Combining with \eqref{e:ZETA.beta.last.error} and \eqref{e:ZETA.qdot.error} then gives
	\[
	\delta_{e,t+1}
	+\ddot{\delta}_{e,t+1}
	\le
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg(
	\frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^k}
	+ \delta_{e,t} 
	+ \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
	\Bigg)\,.
	\]
This concludes our analysis of the update procedure.\smallskip

\noindent\bemph{Part~5. Conclusion.}
Summing the preceding bound over all $e\in\delta v$ gives
	\begin{align*}
	\sum_{t\ge0} (\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t)
	&\le \bm{\delta}_0 + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_0
	+ 
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\sum_{t\ge0} (\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t)
	\le O(\bm{\delta}_0 + \bm{\ddot{\delta}}_0)
	\le O(k 2^k)\,,\\
	\sum_{t\ge0} 
	(\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1})
	&\le 
	\delta_{e,0} + \ddot{\delta}_{e,0}
		+ \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
		 \sum_{t\ge0}
		\Bigg( \frac{\bm{\delta}_t+\bm{\ddot{\delta}}_t}{2^k}+
		\delta_{e,t} + \min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
		\Bigg)
	\le O(1)\,.
	\end{align*}
We can use the above bounds with \eqref{e:ZETA.beta.last.error} to obtain
	\[
	\sum_{t\ge0} \widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4},\hat{q}_{e,t+1})
	\le \begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k} \\ 1 \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\sum_{t\ge0}
	\bigg(\delta_{e,t} + 
			\min\set{\ddot{\delta}_{e,t},1}
			+ \textup{\textsf{err}}_{v,t}\bigg)
	\le \begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k} \\ 1 \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix}
	\frac{k^{O(1)} }{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\]	
Combining with \eqref{e:ZETA.hq.first.error} gives
	\[
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,0},\hat{q}_{e,\infty})
	\le O(1)
	\sum_{t\ge0}\Bigg\{
	\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t},\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4})
	+\widehat{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\hat{q}_{e,t+3/4},\hat{q}_{e,t+1})
	\Bigg\}
	\le
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}
	\begin{pmatrix}
	2^{-k}\\
	1\\
	2^k 
	\end{pmatrix}\,.
	\]
(We also see that 
condition~\eqref{e:condition.on.hat.msg.with.L}
is satisfied by $\hat{q}_{e,t}$ for all $t\ge0$, so that 
the above applications of Proposition~\ref{p:ctypes.varupdate} are justified.)
We also obtain from \eqref{e:ZETA.qdot.error} that
	\[
	\dddot{\textup{\textbf{\textsf{ERR}}}}(\dot{q}_{e,0},\dot{q}_{e,\infty})
	\le
	\begin{pmatrix}
	1\\1\\1\\ 
	2^{-k\epsilon} \\ 1
	\end{pmatrix} 
	\frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\,.
	\]
The above estimates imply that for all $\sigma\in\set{\SSPIN{r},\SSPIN{y},\SSPIN{g},\SSPIN{b}}^2\setminus\set{\SSPIN{r}\SSPIN{r}}$ we have
	\[\mathbf{P}(\sigma_e=\sigma\,|\,\bm{L}_e=\bm{L})
	\cong \dot{q}_{e,\infty}(\sigma\,|\,\bm{L})
		\hat{q}_{e,\infty}(\sigma\,|\,\bm{L})
	= {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\dot{q}_e(\sigma) {}_\star\hspace{-1pt}\hat{q}_e(\sigma)
		\Bigg( 1 + \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg)
	= {}_{*}\omega_e(\sigma)
		\Bigg( 1 + \frac{k^{O(1)}}{2^{k\epsilon}}\Bigg)\,.
	\]
This implies the claimed bounds \eqref{e:balanceMarg}.

nodes.statement: In this lemma we take sigma in the reduced alphabet setSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2. We continue to take varsigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc,SSPINw^2. We write sigmasimvarsigma to indicate compatibility: if sigma^i=SSPINr then varsigma^i=SSPINr; if sigma^iinsetSSPINy,SSPINc then varsigma^iinsetsigma^i,SSPINw. On edge e let mu_0 be a probability measure on pairs (sigma,varsigma) with sigmasimvarsigma, of the form \[ mu_0(sigma,varsigma) =fracIndsigmasimvarsigmaz_0 dotq(sigma) (b_0)^1(sigma^1)(b_0)^2(sigma^2) x_0(varsigma)\,, \] such that mu(sigma^i=tau)=_starhspace-1ptpi_e(tau) for both i=1,2 and all tauinsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc. Assume that _starhspace-1ptpi_e is nice in the sense of Definition~, that dotq(sigma)=Theta(1) for all sigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2, and that b^i(tau)=Theta(1) for i=1,2 and all tauinsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc. Let zeta_0 denote the marginal law of varsigma under mu_0. Let zeta be another probability measure over varsigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc,SSPINw^2 whose single-copy marginals satisfy zeta^1(SSPINr)=_starhspace-1ptpi_e(SSPINr)=zeta^2(SSPINr). Assume that maxbigg\ 1-zeta_0(SSPINwSSPINw), 1-zeta(SSPINwSSPINw)bigg\ &le frack^O(1)2^k\,,\\ hatiota equiv frack^44^k + maxbigg\ zeta_0(setSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2), zeta(setSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2) bigg\ &le frac12^k(1+epsilon)\,. Assume moreover that we have parameters delta le O(1) and ddotdeltale 2^k(1-epsilon) such that max Bigg\ Big|zeta(varsigma)-zeta_0(varsigma)Big| : varsigmainset SSPINrSSPINw,SSPINySSPINw,SSPINcSSPINw, SSPINwSSPINr,SSPINwSSPINy,SSPINwSSPINc Bigg\ &le frack^O(1)delta2^k\,,\\ max Bigg\ Big|zeta(varsigma)-zeta_0(varsigma)Big| : varsigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2 Bigg\ &le hatiota delta\,, \\ bigg| fraczeta(SSPINrSSPINr) zeta_0(SSPINrSSPINr)-1bigg| &leddotdelta\,. Then there exist weights (b_3/4)^1, (b_3/4)^2, x_3/4 such that under the corresponding measure mu_3/4 (see ) the spin varsigma has marginal zeta_3/4=zeta. Moreover, if we let hatz_t be the normalizing constant such that \[ hatq_t(sigma) = frac1hatz_t (b_t)^1(sigma^1)(b_t)^2(sigma^2) sum_varsigma:varsigmasimsigma x_t(varsigma) \] is a probability measure, then the new weights can be chosen such that the error between hatq_0 and hatq_3/4 is very small: \[ widehattextupfootnotesize ERR(hatq_0,hatq_3/4) le k^O(1) hatiota & 0 \\ 2^khatiota &0 \\ 1& 1 delta \\ ddotdelta \,,\] using the notation of Definition~. We begin with some easy observations. By the assumption that dotq=Theta(1) and b^i=Theta(1), we have \[ mu_0(sigma,varsigma) = fracIndsigmasimvarsigma z_0 Theta(1) x(varsigma)\,. \] It then follows from and that x(SSPINwSSPINw)/z_0ge 1-k^O(1)/2^k, while maxBigg\ fracx(varsigma)z_0 : varsigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc,SSPINw^2 setminussetSSPINwSSPINw Bigg\ &le frack^O(1)2^k\,,\\ maxBigg\ fracx(varsigma)z_0 : varsigmainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2 Bigg\ le O(hatiota) &le fracO(1)2^k(1+epsilon)\,. This implies that mu_0(sigma)=Theta(1) for all sigmainsetSSPINy,SSPINc^2, since in this case \[ mu_0(sigma) =frac1z_0bigg\ Theta(1) x(SSPINwSSPINw) + frack^O(1)2^kbigg\ =Theta(1)\,. \] Next, by the assumption that _starhspace-1ptpi_e is nice and mu_0 is judicious, we have \[ fracTheta(1)2^k = _starhspace-1ptpi_e(SSPINr) = mu_0(sigma^1=SSPINr) = fracTheta(1)z_0 sum_varthetain setSSPINrtimessetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc,SSPINw x(vartheta) = fracTheta(1)x(SSPINrSSPINw)z_0 + fracO(1)2^k(1+epsilon)\,, \] which shows that x(SSPINrSSPINw)=Theta(2^-k). It follows from this that \[ mu_0(sigma=vartheta) = fracTheta(1)2^k textupfor all varthetainsetSSPINrSSPINy,SSPINrSSPINc, SSPINySSPINr,SSPINcSSPINr\,. \] Lastly, we note that directly implies mu_0(sigma=SSPINrSSPINr) =zeta_0(SSPINrSSPINr) le 2^-k(1+epsilon). In summary we have seen that the assumptions of the lemma imply mu_0(sigma=vartheta) = Theta(1) & textupif SSPINr[vartheta]=0,\\ Theta(2^-k) & textupif SSPINr[vartheta]=1,\\ O(2^-k(1+epsilon)) & textupif SSPINr[vartheta]=2, for varthetainsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc^2. bemphPart 1. Description of update procedure. We will define a sequence of weights (b_t)^i, x_t ending with the desired weights at t= 3/4. For each t denote the corresponding measure mu_t(sigma,varsigma) =fracIndsigmasimvarsigmaz_t dotq(sigma) (b_t)^1(sigma^1)(b_t)^2(sigma^2) x_t(varsigma)\,, with z_t the normalizing constant. Let zeta_t denote the marginal law of varsigma under mu_t. [(a)] item Time t=0 to t=1/4. First adjust the weight on varsigma=SSPINySSPINw: set frac(b_1/4)^1(SSPINy)(b_0)^1(SSPINy) &= fracmu_0(sigma^1=SSPINy)-zeta(SSPINySSPINw) mu_0(sigma^1=SSPINy)-mu_0(varsigma=SSPINySSPINw) \,,\\ fracx_1/4(SSPINySSPINw)x_0(SSPINySSPINw) &= fracmu_0(sigma^1=SSPINy) -mu_0(varsigma=SSPINySSPINw) mu_0(sigma^1=SSPINy)-zeta(SSPINySSPINw) fraczeta(SSPINySSPINw)mu_0(varsigma=SSPINySSPINw)\,. We call and the bemphSSPINySSPINw-update. At the same time also make the updates and with SSPINc in place of SSPINy, to define new weights (b_1/4)^1(SSPINc) and x_1/4(SSPINcSSPINw) --- we call this the bemphSSPINcSSPINw-update. Keep all the other weights unchanged, that is, (b_1/4)^1(SSPINr)=(b_0)^1(SSPINr), (b_1/4)^2(tau)=(b_0)^1(tau) for all tauinsetSSPINr,SSPINy,SSPINc, and x_1/4(varsigma)=x_0(varsigma) for all varsigma notinsetSSPINySSPINw,SSPINcSSPINw. item Time t=1/4 to t=1/2. Perform the analogous update in the second copy: for the bemphSSPINwSSPINy-update, set frac(b_1/2)^2(SSPINy)(b_1/4)^2(SSPINy) &= fracmu_1/4(sigma^2=SSPINy)-zeta(SSPINwSSPINy) mu_1/4(sigma^2=SSPINy) -mu_1/4(varsigma=SSPINwSSPINy) \,,\\ fracx_1/2(SSPINwSSPINy)x_1/4(SSPINwSSPINy) &= fracmu_1/4(sigma^2=SSPINy) -mu_1/4(varsigma=SSPINwSSPINy) mu_1/4(sigma^2=SSPINy)-zeta(SSPINwSSPINy) fraczeta(SSPINwSSPINy) mu_1/4(varsigma=SSPINwSSPINy)\,. Likewise make the bemphSSPINwSSPINc-update, to define new weights (b_1/2)^2(SSPINc) and x_1/2(SSPINwSSPINc). Again, keep all the other weights unchanged. item Time t=1/2 to t=3/4. The remainder of the proof is outlined as follows: [--] item In hyperlinkl:DIVERSE.product.PaPart 1 we define a measure P^a satisfying constraints , , and , where is a relaxation of . We show that P^a has a simple explicit form, and has substantially larger entropy than P (see below). item In hyperlinkl:DIDERSE.Pa.boundsPart 2 we prove probabilistic estimates on various quantities under the measure P^a. Let X^a denote a sample from P^a; in the rest of the proof we transform X^a without changing its frozen spin x=x^ainsetSPIN-,SPIN+,SPINf^2. item In hyperlinkl:DIVERSE.PbPart 3 we transform X^a into X^b, and in hyperlinkl:DIVERSE.PcPart 4 we transform X^b into X^c. The goal of this step is to create enough SPINwhite spins which can be altered in the next step to ensure that the constraints or will be satisfied. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{l:expand.on.types}
nodes.statement: We first show that in the original textupk-textscsat graph G'=(V',F',E')simP=P_n,m, bemphevery subset of variables Ssubseteq V' satisfies the bound |F_bullet(S)|le n 2^29k/30/k & textupif 0 le |S|/n le 4/5,\\ |S| &textupif c_1/2 le |S|/n le 1/4, where c_1 is as in Proposition~. (Note that refers to the number |V| of variables in the processed graph, while in and throughout this proof we use nequiv |V'|ge|V| to refer to the number of variables in the original graph. Thus in we crudely divided the first bound by a factor k, which we will use below to account for the discrepancy in the number of variables in G' versus in G.) Towards the proof of , recall that F_bullet(S) denotes the subset of clauses ain F with |Scap partial a|ge 9k/10. Note that for any fixed subset Ssubseteq V' of size |S|=ns, the probability that a particular clause ain F' belongs to F_bullet(S) is given by \[ p_s = Pbigg( textupBin(k,s) ge frac9k10bigg) le exp Bigg\ -kHbigg(frac910\,bigg|\,sbigg) Bigg\ le 2^-k/20&textupfor all 0le sle 4/5,\\ s^2k/3&textupfor all 0le sle 1/4, \] where the first inequality is from the Chernoff bound and the second is by direct comparison. nodes.name: Proof of Proposition~\ref{p:apriori}
nodes.statement: If D expands on type-subsets, then Proposition~ yields that all non-defective variables are diverse, and all strongly non-defective clauses are light. Moreover, since a non-defective clause can neighbor at most one defective variable, it follows that every non-defective clause is diverse in the sense of Definition~. Thus, if a variable v is strongly non-defective, then all the clauses around it must be both diverse and light, meaning cancelD(v)=cancelL(v)=0. Proposition~ then gives the desired estimate (by taking zeta_*=epsilon_circ) for omega_bmL,j whenever bmL(j) is a strongly non-defective edge type.

	\[\mathbb{E}\Bigg(

The bound certainly holds for $\ell=0$, where we have
$\dot{\eta}^\ell=\ddot{\eta}^\ell=1/2$ with probability one. Suppose inductively that the bound holds for $\ell-1\ge0$. Define the i.i.d.\ array
	\[\vec{t}\equiv\bigg(
		(t^\SPIN{+}_{ij}, t^\SPIN{-}_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}
		\bigg)
	\]
where each entry $t=(\dot{t},\ddot{t})$ is an independent sample from the monotone coupling ${\textup{\textsf{\footnotesize PGW}}}(\dot{\alpha},\ddot{\alpha})$. Let
	\begin{equation}\label{e:array.coupled.trees.a}
	\vec{a}
	\equiv \bigg( 
		(a^\SPIN{+}_{ij},a^\SPIN{-}_{ij})_{i,j\ge1} \bigg)
	\end{equation}
where each entry $a=(\dot{\eta},\ddot{\eta})$ is obtained by applying the map $\bm{F}_{\ell-1}$ to the corresponding entry in $\vec{t}$: that is,
	\[
	a^\SPIN{+}_{ij}
	\equiv (\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{+}_{ij},
	\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{+}_{ij})
	\equiv \Bigg(
		\Big[\bm{F}_{\ell-1}
		(\dot{t}^\SPIN{+}_{ij})\Big](\SPIN{-}),
		\Big[\bm{F}_{\ell-1}
		(\ddot{t}^\SPIN{+}_{ij})\Big](\SPIN{-})
		\Bigg)
	\in[0,1)^2\,.
	\]
Next, let
$\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm},\delta^\SPIN{\textpm}$ be independent random variables with
	\[
	\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}\bigg( \frac{\dot{\alpha}k}{2}\bigg)\,,\quad
	\delta^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}\bigg( \frac{
		(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})
		k}{2}\bigg)\,.
	\]
Let $\ddot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}\equiv

	\,\mathbb{E}\Bigg( 
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[ (\dot{s}^\SPIN{-}_1-\ddot{s}^\SPIN{-}_1)^2
			\,\bigg|\,
			\dot{T}\bigg]^2
			\Bigg)\,,\]
where the first factor is $\le k^{O(1)}$ because $\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}$ is well concentrated around $k\dot{\alpha}/2$ while each $\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]$ is well concentrated around $1/2^k$
(using Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds} again). For the second factor, we can bound
	\[(\dot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i-\ddot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i)^2
	\le k\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]^2 
		(\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
			-\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij} )^2\,,\quad
	u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]
	\equiv \prod_{j'=1}^{j-1}
		\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij'}
		\prod_{j'=j+1}^{k-1}
		\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij'}\,.\]
Combining with the inductive hypothesis gives
	\[\mathbb{E}\Bigg(\mathbb{E}\bigg[(\dot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i-\ddot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i)^2
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}
		\bigg]^2
		\Bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
	{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}
		\Bigg\{\max_{1\le j\le k-1}
		\mathbb{E}[ u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]^4 ]
		\Bigg\}
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}{
		2^{8k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.\]

	\[\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[ (\dot{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-}
		-\tilde{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-})^2 
		\,\bigg|\, \dot{T} \bigg]^2
	\Bigg)
	=\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[ 
	\Bigg(
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}} 
	(\dot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i-
	\ddot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i)
	\Bigg)^2 
		\,\Bigg|\, \dot{T} \Bigg]^2
	\Bigg)
	\le 
	\mathbb{E}\Big[ (\dot{d}^\SPIN{-})^2\Big]
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[ (\dot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i-
	\ddot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i)^2\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\Bigg)\,.\]
By a similar derivation as for \eqref{e:telescoping.sum.u.h}, we can bound
	 \[\mathbb{E}\Bigg(\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	(\dot{X}^\SPIN{-}_1 -
		\ddot{X}^\SPIN{-}_1)^2
	\,\bigg|\, \dot{T} \bigg]^2\Bigg)
	\le k^3
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\bigg(\frac{u[j]}{1-u[j]}\bigg)^4
	\Bigg)
	\,\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[(\eta_j-\tilde\eta_j)^2 \,\bigg|\, \dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\Bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}{
		2^{8k} / k^{O(1)}}\,,\]
where the last step again uses the inductive hypothesis together with Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}.
Altogether we obtain
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(
		\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{a}^2
		\,\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2\bigg)
	\le 
	\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}{ 2^{4k}/k^{O(1)}}.\]
Combining with the bound on $\mathbf{A}$
verifies the inductive hypothesis, concluding the proof.
