		\,\Big|\, \dot{T} \Big]^2
	\Bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{3k}/k^{O(1)}}\]
for all $\ell\ge0$.

\begin{proof}
We will argue by induction, using the same notation as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim}. The bound clearly holds for $\ell=0$, so suppose it holds for $\ell-1\ge0$. Decompose 
$\ddot{\eta}^\ell-\dot{\eta}^\ell =\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{a}$ as in \eqref{e:diff.eta.terms}. Applying
the bound \eqref{e:F.second.derivs} from Lemma~\ref{l:F.bounds.calculus} gives
	\[
	\mathbf{a} 
	=\overbrace{\bigg\{
	\Big( \tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-} \Big)
	F_x(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
	\bigg\}}^{\textup{denote this }\mathbf{a}_x}
	{}+{}
	\overbrace{\bigg\{
	(\tilde{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma})
	F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
	\bigg\}}^{\textup{denote this }\mathbf{a}_y}
	{}+{}
	\overbrace{O\bigg(
	(\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-})^2
	\bigg)}^{\textup{denote this }\mathbf{a}_{xx}}
	{}+{}
	\overbrace{
	O\bigg(
	\Big(\tilde{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}\Big)^2
	\bigg)
	}^{\textup{denote this }\mathbf{a}_{yy}}\,.
	\]
We deal with each term separately in what follows.\smallskip

\noindent\bemph{Bound on $\mathbf{a}_x$.} Let $\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]$ and $u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]$ be as defined in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim}. Then we have
	\[\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}
	=
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}
	\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i] (\ddot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i
		-\dot{s}^\SPIN{-}_i)
	=
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}
	\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]
	(\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
	-\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})\,.\]
Meanwhile, $F_x(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})$ is a measurable function of $\dot{T}$, 
and from Lemma~\ref{l:F.bounds.calculus} we have $|F_x(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})|\le1$. Combining with the inductive hypothesis, together with the independence of the random subtrees, we have
	\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{a}_x\,\Big|\,\dot{T}
		\Big]^2\bigg)
	&\le\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\Bigg\{
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]
		u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\bigg]
		\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		(\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
		-\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\bigg]
	\Bigg\}^2
	\Bigg)
	\\
	&\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{3k}/k^{O(1)}}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\dot{d}^\SPIN{-} k
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]
		u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\Bigg) \le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{3k}/k^{O(1)}}\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last inequality uses the estimates from Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}.\smallskip

	
\noindent\bemph{Bound on $\mathbf{a}_y$.} For this part of the proof we will generate the pair $(\dot{T},\ddot{T})$ in a slightly different way, as follows. We take the subtrees $\dot{t}_{ij}$ and $\ddot{t}_{ij}$ as before; the only difference is in the $\SPIN{\textpm}$-degrees of the root variable $v_\textup{\textsc{rt}}$. Let $d\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}(k\dot{\alpha})$, and $\delta\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}(k(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha}))$.
Let $S_i$ be i.i.d.\ symmetric random signs, and let
	\[
	\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\equiv
	\sum_{i=1}^d \Ind{S_i=\SPIN{\textpm}}\,,\quad
	\ddot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\equiv
	\sum_{i=1}^{d+\delta} \Ind{S_i=\SPIN{\textpm}}\,.
	\]
We then let $v_\textup{\textsc{rt}}$ have $\SPIN{\textpm}$-degrees $\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}$ in $\dot{T}$, and $\ddot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}$ in $\ddot{T}$. Then, similarly to \eqref{e:telescoping.sum.u.h} we can decompose
	\[
	\tilde{\Sigma}
	-\dot{\Sigma}
	=\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		(\ddot{X}_i - \dot{X}_i)
	= -\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\ln\frac{1-u_i[j]\ddot{\eta}_{ij}}
		{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}}\,.
	\]
Note in the above that $\dot{X}_i$ stands for $\dot{X}^\SPIN{+}_i$ or $\dot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i$ depending on the sign $S_i$, but we have dropped the superscripts for notational convenience. Applying the approximation
	\[
	f(\eta)
	=\ln\frac1{1-u_i[j]\eta}
	=f(\eta_0)
	+(\eta-\eta_0)f'(\eta_0)
	+O\bigg( \|f''\|_\infty
	(\eta-\eta_0)^2 \bigg)
	\]
gives the following expansion for $\mathbf{a}_y$:
	\[\mathbf{a}_y
	=
	\overbrace{\Bigg(
	-F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
		\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\frac{u_i[j] (\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})}
		{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}}
		\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote
			 this }
			\mathbf{a}_{y,1}}
	{} + {} O\overbrace{\Bigg(\sum_{i=1}^d
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\Big(\frac{u_i[j]
		(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
		}{1-u_i[j]}\Big)^2
		\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote
			 this }
			\mathbf{a}_{y,2}}\,.
	\]
We bound these terms separately, beginning with the quadratic term $\mathbf{a}_{y,2}$:
	\[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,2}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\le dk
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
		\bigg(\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]}\bigg)^2
		\,\Bigg|\, \dot{T}\Bigg]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})^2
			\,\Big|
			\,\dot{T}_{ij}\Big]^2\,.
	\]
Combining with the inductive hypothesis,
Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}, and Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim} gives
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,2}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\bigg)
	\le\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.\]
We next bound the contribution from the linear term $\mathbf{a}_{y,1}$, which requires some more care. Expanding $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$ as a double sum over indices $1\le i_1,i_2\le d$, we first bound the contribution from the cross terms $i_1\ne i_2$. Here the issue is that although $S_{i_1}S_{i_2}$ certainly has mean zero, 
 the cross term may not have mean zero because of the factor $F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})^2$ which is correlated with $S_{i_1},S_{i_2}$. However we shall argue that this effect is negligible. To this end, we shall approximate $\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}$ and $\dot{\Sigma}$ by
	\[\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]
	\equiv \prod_{\substack{i \in
		[\dot{d}]
		\setminus \set{i_1,i_2},\\
		S_i=\SPIN{-} }}
		\dot{s}_i, \quad
	\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]
	\equiv
	\sum_{\substack{i \in
		[\dot{d}]
		\setminus \set{i_1,i_2} }}
		S_i X_i\,.\]
Let $H(x,y) \equiv F_y(x,y)^2$, and note that
for $0\le x\le1$ and $xe^y\le1$ we have
	\begin{align*}
	|H_x(x,y)| 
	&= 2 \cdot \Bigg| 
	\frac{(1-x)e^y}{(1+(1-x)e^y)^3}
	\frac{1-(1-x)e^y}{1+(1-x)e^y}
	\frac{e^y}{(1-xe^y)+ e^y}
	\Bigg|
	\le2\,,\\
	|H_y(x,y)|
	&= 2 \cdot\Bigg|
	\bigg(\frac{(1-x)e^y}{(1+(1-x)e^y)^2}\bigg)^2
	\frac{1-(1-x)e^y}{1+(1-x)e^y}
	\Bigg|
	\le2\,.
	\end{align*}
It follows that, abbreviating 
$H[i_1i_2]
	\equiv
	H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2],\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2])$, we have
	\[
	\Big|H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
	-H[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\le
	2\Bigg\{
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+ 
	\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\Bigg\}\,.
	\]
Returning to the expression for $\mathbf{a}_{y,1}$, 
let us denote
	\[\bm{T}(i)
	\equiv\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]
		\dot{\eta}_{ij} }
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T} \bigg]\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
	\,\Big|\, \dot{T}
	\Big]\,.\]
We then use the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality to bound
	\[
	\bm{T}(i)^2
	\le
	k \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} 
	\overbrace{\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]}
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T} \bigg]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
	\,\Big|\, \dot{T}
	\Big]^2
	\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote this } \bm{T}(ij)^2}\,.
	\]
Using the inductive hypothesis and Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}, the $i_1,i_2$ cross term in $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$ can be bounded by
	\begin{align*}
	&\overbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		H[i_1i_2]
	\prod_{l=1}^2 \Big\{ S_{i_l} \bm{T}(i_l)\Big\}
		\Bigg)}^\text{zero}
	+
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\Big( H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},
	\dot{\Sigma}) - H[i_1i_2]\Big)
	\prod_{l=1}^2 \Big\{ S_{i_l} \bm{T}(i_l)\Big\}
		\Bigg] \\
	&=O(1)
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\bigg\{
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\bigg\}
	\sum_{l=1}^2
	\bm{T}(i_l)^2
	\Big]\Bigg]\\
	&\le
	\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{3k} / k^{O(1)}}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\bigg(
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\bigg)
	\sum_{l=1}^2
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_{i_l}[j]}{1-u_{i_l}[j]}
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\setminus\dot{T}_{ij}
		\bigg]^2
	\Bigg]
	\le\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{6k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.
	\end{align*}
The total contribution to
$\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$
from cross terms $i_1\ne i_2$ is thus
$ \le k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 / 2^{4k}$, so
	\begin{align*}
	&\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\bigg)
	\le\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}
		+ \mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})^2
		\sum_{i=1}^d 
		\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\frac{u_i[j] (\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij}) }
			{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}} 
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}
		\bigg]^2
	\Bigg) \\
	&\le
	\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k}/k^{O(1)}}
	+ k\, \mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		\sum_{i=1}^d 
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\frac{u_i[j] }
			{1-u_i[j]} 
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}
		\bigg]^2
		\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
		\,\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\Bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k}/k^{O(1)}}\,,
	\end{align*}
having again used the inductive hypothesis
together with Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}.

\smallskip\noindent\bemph{Bounds
	on $\mathbf{a}_{xx}$ and $\mathbf{a}_{yy}$.}
The quadratic terms are more straightforward to bound:
	\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{xx}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	(\dot{d}^\SPIN{-})^3
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
		\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]^2
		u_i[j]^2
		\,\Big|\,
		\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
		-\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})^2\,
	\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\bigg)\,,\\
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{yy}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	d^3 \sum_{k=1}^d \sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\Big(
		\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]} \Big)^2
		\,\bigg|\, \dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\,\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
		-\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})^2\,
	\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\Bigg)\,.
	\end{align*}
Combining with
Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds} and 
 Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim} gives
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{xx}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	+\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{yy}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,.
	\]
This concludes our bounds for $\mathbf{a}$.\smallskip



\noindent\bemph{Bound on $\mathbf{A}$.}
Recall that the tree $\dot{T}$
has root degree $\dot{d}$
while $\ddot{T}$
has root degree $\ddot{d}\equiv \dot{d} + \delta$.
Let $\tilde{T}$ be the subtree of $\ddot{T}$
formed by deleting all subtrees descended
from root neighbors
with indices larger than $\dot{d}$,
so that $\dot{T}\subseteq\tilde{T}\subseteq\ddot{T}$.
By Jensen's inequality,
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\bigg)
	\le \mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\tilde{T}]^2\bigg)\,.
	\]
If $\ddot{d}=\dot{d}$ then clearly $\mathbf{A}=0$. Since $|\mathbf{A}|\le1$ almost surely, we can bound
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{A}\Ind{\delta\ge2}
		\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2\bigg)
	\le \mathbb{P}(\delta\ge2)^2
	\le k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^4\,.\]
On the event $\delta=1$, applying the bound
\eqref{e:F.second.derivs} from Lemma~\ref{l:F.bounds.calculus} gives
	\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{A}\Ind{\delta=1}
		\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]
	&=\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\overbrace{
	\bigg\{
	F_x(\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\tilde{\Sigma})
	\Big(\ddot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-} -\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}\Big)
	\bigg\}
	}^{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_x}
	+\overbrace{
	\bigg\{
	F_y(\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\tilde{\Sigma})
	\Big(\ddot{\Sigma}-
		\tilde{\Sigma}\Big)
	\bigg\}}^{\textup{denote this }
		\bar{\mathbf{A}}_y}\\
	&\qquad\qquad\qquad+
	\underbrace{
	O\bigg(
	(\ddot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-} -
		\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-})^2
	\bigg)}_{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{xx}}
	+\underbrace{
	O\bigg(
	(\ddot{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-} -
		\tilde{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-})^2
	\bigg)}_{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{yy}}
	\Bigg]\,.
	\end{align*}
Since $\delta=1$
with probability $ O(k) (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})$,
we find
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_x
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2
		\mathbb{E}[ (\tilde\Pi^\SPIN{-})^2 ]}
		{ 2^{2k} / k^{O(1)} }
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,,\]
and by similar considerations
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(
		\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{xx}
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	+\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{yy}
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.
	\]
Finally, by symmetry,
$\mathbb{E}[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_y\,|\,\tilde{T}]=0$.
Altogether this yields
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\Big]
	\le 
	k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^4
	+\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }
	\le\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,,
	\]
where the last step uses the assumed bound on $\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha}$.

\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Conclusion.}
Substituting the above estimates into \eqref{e:diff.eta.terms} gives
the claimed bound.
\end{proof}

	\Bigg)
	\\
	&\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{3k}/k^{O(1)}}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	\dot{d}^\SPIN{-} k
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]
		u^\SPIN{-}_i[j]
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\Bigg) \le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{3k}/k^{O(1)}}\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last inequality uses the estimates from Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}.\smallskip

	
\noindent\bemph{Bound on $\mathbf{a}_y$.} For this part of the proof we will generate the pair $(\dot{T},\ddot{T})$ in a slightly different way, as follows. We take the subtrees $\dot{t}_{ij}$ and $\ddot{t}_{ij}$ as before; the only difference is in the $\SPIN{\textpm}$-degrees of the root variable $v_\textup{\textsc{rt}}$. Let $d\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}(k\dot{\alpha})$, and $\delta\sim\textup{\textsf{Pois}}(k(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha}))$.
Let $S_i$ be i.i.d.\ symmetric random signs, and let
	\[
	\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\equiv
	\sum_{i=1}^d \Ind{S_i=\SPIN{\textpm}}\,,\quad
	\ddot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}
	\equiv
	\sum_{i=1}^{d+\delta} \Ind{S_i=\SPIN{\textpm}}\,.
	\]
We then let $v_\textup{\textsc{rt}}$ have $\SPIN{\textpm}$-degrees $\dot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}$ in $\dot{T}$, and $\ddot{d}^\SPIN{\textpm}$ in $\ddot{T}$. Then, similarly to \eqref{e:telescoping.sum.u.h} we can decompose
	\[
	\tilde{\Sigma}
	-\dot{\Sigma}
	=\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		(\ddot{X}_i - \dot{X}_i)
	= -\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\ln\frac{1-u_i[j]\ddot{\eta}_{ij}}
		{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}}\,.
	\]
Note in the above that $\dot{X}_i$ stands for $\dot{X}^\SPIN{+}_i$ or $\dot{X}^\SPIN{-}_i$ depending on the sign $S_i$, but we have dropped the superscripts for notational convenience. Applying the approximation
	\[
	f(\eta)
	=\ln\frac1{1-u_i[j]\eta}
	=f(\eta_0)
	+(\eta-\eta_0)f'(\eta_0)
	+O\bigg( \|f''\|_\infty
	(\eta-\eta_0)^2 \bigg)
	\]
gives the following expansion for $\mathbf{a}_y$:
	\[\mathbf{a}_y
	=
	\overbrace{\Bigg(
	-F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
		\sum_{i=1}^d S_i
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\frac{u_i[j] (\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})}
		{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}}
		\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote
			 this }
			\mathbf{a}_{y,1}}
	{} + {} O\overbrace{\Bigg(\sum_{i=1}^d
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\Big(\frac{u_i[j]
		(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
		}{1-u_i[j]}\Big)^2
		\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote
			 this }
			\mathbf{a}_{y,2}}\,.
	\]
We bound these terms separately, beginning with the quadratic term $\mathbf{a}_{y,2}$:
	\[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,2}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\le dk
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
		\bigg(\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]}\bigg)^2
		\,\Bigg|\, \dot{T}\Bigg]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})^2
			\,\Big|
			\,\dot{T}_{ij}\Big]^2\,.
	\]
Combining with the inductive hypothesis,
Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}, and Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim} gives
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,2}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\bigg)
	\le\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.\]
We next bound the contribution from the linear term $\mathbf{a}_{y,1}$, which requires some more care. Expanding $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$ as a double sum over indices $1\le i_1,i_2\le d$, we first bound the contribution from the cross terms $i_1\ne i_2$. Here the issue is that although $S_{i_1}S_{i_2}$ certainly has mean zero, 
 the cross term may not have mean zero because of the factor $F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})^2$ which is correlated with $S_{i_1},S_{i_2}$. However we shall argue that this effect is negligible. To this end, we shall approximate $\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}$ and $\dot{\Sigma}$ by
	\[\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]
	\equiv \prod_{\substack{i \in
		[\dot{d}]
		\setminus \set{i_1,i_2},\\
		S_i=\SPIN{-} }}
		\dot{s}_i, \quad
	\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]
	\equiv
	\sum_{\substack{i \in
		[\dot{d}]
		\setminus \set{i_1,i_2} }}
		S_i X_i\,.\]
Let $H(x,y) \equiv F_y(x,y)^2$, and note that
for $0\le x\le1$ and $xe^y\le1$ we have
	\begin{align*}
	|H_x(x,y)| 
	&= 2 \cdot \Bigg| 
	\frac{(1-x)e^y}{(1+(1-x)e^y)^3}
	\frac{1-(1-x)e^y}{1+(1-x)e^y}
	\frac{e^y}{(1-xe^y)+ e^y}
	\Bigg|
	\le2\,,\\
	|H_y(x,y)|
	&= 2 \cdot\Bigg|
	\bigg(\frac{(1-x)e^y}{(1+(1-x)e^y)^2}\bigg)^2
	\frac{1-(1-x)e^y}{1+(1-x)e^y}
	\Bigg|
	\le2\,.
	\end{align*}
It follows that, abbreviating 
$H[i_1i_2]
	\equiv
	H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2],\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2])$, we have
	\[
	\Big|H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})
	-H[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\le
	2\Bigg\{
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+ 
	\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\Bigg\}\,.
	\]
Returning to the expression for $\mathbf{a}_{y,1}$, 
let us denote
	\[\bm{T}(i)
	\equiv\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]
		\dot{\eta}_{ij} }
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T} \bigg]\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
	\,\Big|\, \dot{T}
	\Big]\,.\]
We then use the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality to bound
	\[
	\bm{T}(i)^2
	\le
	k \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} 
	\overbrace{\Bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]}
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T} \bigg]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
	\,\Big|\, \dot{T}
	\Big]^2
	\Bigg)}^{\textup{denote this } \bm{T}(ij)^2}\,.
	\]
Using the inductive hypothesis and Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}, the $i_1,i_2$ cross term in $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$ can be bounded by
	\begin{align*}
	&\overbrace{\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		H[i_1i_2]
	\prod_{l=1}^2 \Big\{ S_{i_l} \bm{T}(i_l)\Big\}
		\Bigg)}^\text{zero}
	+
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\Big( H(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},
	\dot{\Sigma}) - H[i_1i_2]\Big)
	\prod_{l=1}^2 \Big\{ S_{i_l} \bm{T}(i_l)\Big\}
		\Bigg] \\
	&=O(1)
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\bigg\{
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\bigg\}
	\sum_{l=1}^2
	\bm{T}(i_l)^2
	\Big]\Bigg]\\
	&\le
	\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{3k} / k^{O(1)}}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\bigg(
	\Big|\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}-\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	+\Big|\dot{\Sigma}-\dot{\Sigma}[i_1i_2]\Big|
	\bigg)
	\sum_{l=1}^2
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
	\frac{u_{i_l}[j]}{1-u_{i_l}[j]}
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}\setminus\dot{T}_{ij}
		\bigg]^2
	\Bigg]
	\le\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{6k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.
	\end{align*}
The total contribution to
$\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2]$
from cross terms $i_1\ne i_2$ is thus
$ \le k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 / 2^{4k}$, so
	\begin{align*}
	&\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{y,1}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\bigg)
	\le\frac{ (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2 }
		{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}
		+ \mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		F_y(\dot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\dot{\Sigma})^2
		\sum_{i=1}^d 
		\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\frac{u_i[j] (\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij}) }
			{1-u_i[j]\dot{\eta}_{ij}} 
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}
		\bigg]^2
	\Bigg) \\
	&\le
	\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k}/k^{O(1)}}
	+ k\, \mathbb{E}\Bigg(
		\sum_{i=1}^d 
		\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
		\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\frac{u_i[j] }
			{1-u_i[j]} 
		\,\bigg|\,\dot{T}
		\bigg]^2
		\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}_{ij}-\dot{\eta}_{ij})
		\,\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\Bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k}/k^{O(1)}}\,,
	\end{align*}
having again used the inductive hypothesis
together with Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds}.

\smallskip\noindent\bemph{Bounds
	on $\mathbf{a}_{xx}$ and $\mathbf{a}_{yy}$.}
The quadratic terms are more straightforward to bound:
	\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{xx}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	(\dot{d}^\SPIN{-})^3
	\sum_{i=1}^{\dot{d}^\SPIN{-}}
	\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
		\Pi^\SPIN{-}[i]^2
		u_i[j]^2
		\,\Big|\,
		\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\,
	\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
		-\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})^2\,
	\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\bigg)\,,\\
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{yy}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	&\le k^{O(1)}
	\mathbb{E}\Bigg(
	d^3 \sum_{k=1}^d \sum_{j=1}^{k-1}
	\mathbb{E}\bigg[
		\Big(
		\frac{u_i[j]}{1-u_i[j]} \Big)^2
		\,\bigg|\, \dot{T}\bigg]^2
	\,\mathbb{E}\Big[(\ddot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij}
		-\dot{\eta}^\SPIN{-}_{ij})^2\,
	\Big|\,\dot{T}\Big]^2
	\Bigg)\,.
	\end{align*}
Combining with
Lemma~\ref{l:X.tail.bounds} and 
 Lemma~\ref{lem-Q-monotone-coupling-prelim} gives
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{xx}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	+\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{a}_{yy}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\Big]
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,.
	\]
This concludes our bounds for $\mathbf{a}$.\smallskip



\noindent\bemph{Bound on $\mathbf{A}$.}
Recall that the tree $\dot{T}$
has root degree $\dot{d}$
while $\ddot{T}$
has root degree $\ddot{d}\equiv \dot{d} + \delta$.
Let $\tilde{T}$ be the subtree of $\ddot{T}$
formed by deleting all subtrees descended
from root neighbors
with indices larger than $\dot{d}$,
so that $\dot{T}\subseteq\tilde{T}\subseteq\ddot{T}$.
By Jensen's inequality,
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2\bigg)
	\le \mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\tilde{T}]^2\bigg)\,.
	\]
If $\ddot{d}=\dot{d}$ then clearly $\mathbf{A}=0$. Since $|\mathbf{A}|\le1$ almost surely, we can bound
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(
	\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{A}\Ind{\delta\ge2}
		\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2\bigg)
	\le \mathbb{P}(\delta\ge2)^2
	\le k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^4\,.\]
On the event $\delta=1$, applying the bound
\eqref{e:F.second.derivs} from Lemma~\ref{l:F.bounds.calculus} gives
	\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{E}\Big[\mathbf{A}\Ind{\delta=1}
		\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]
	&=\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
	\overbrace{
	\bigg\{
	F_x(\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\tilde{\Sigma})
	\Big(\ddot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-} -\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-}\Big)
	\bigg\}
	}^{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_x}
	+\overbrace{
	\bigg\{
	F_y(\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-},\tilde{\Sigma})
	\Big(\ddot{\Sigma}-
		\tilde{\Sigma}\Big)
	\bigg\}}^{\textup{denote this }
		\bar{\mathbf{A}}_y}\\
	&\qquad\qquad\qquad+
	\underbrace{
	O\bigg(
	(\ddot{\Pi}^\SPIN{-} -
		\tilde{\Pi}^\SPIN{-})^2
	\bigg)}_{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{xx}}
	+\underbrace{
	O\bigg(
	(\ddot{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-} -
		\tilde{\Sigma}^\SPIN{-})^2
	\bigg)}_{\textup{denote this }\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{yy}}
	\Bigg]\,.
	\end{align*}
Since $\delta=1$
with probability $ O(k) (\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})$,
we find
	\[\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_x
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2
		\mathbb{E}[ (\tilde\Pi^\SPIN{-})^2 ]}
		{ 2^{2k} / k^{O(1)} }
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,,\]
and by similar considerations
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\bigg(
		\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{xx}
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	+\mathbb{E}\bigg(\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_{yy}
		\Ind{\delta=1}\,\Big|\,\tilde{T}\Big]^2
		\bigg)
	\le \frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{2^{4k} / k^{O(1)}}\,.
	\]
Finally, by symmetry,
$\mathbb{E}[\bar{\mathbf{A}}_y\,|\,\tilde{T}]=0$.
Altogether this yields
	\[
	\mathbb{E}\Big[
	\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{A}\,|\,\dot{T}]^2
	\Big]
	\le 
	k^{O(1)}(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^4
	+\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }
	\le\frac{(\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha})^2}
		{ 2^{4k} / k^{O(1)} }\,,
	\]
where the last step uses the assumed bound on $\ddot{\alpha}-\dot{\alpha}$.

\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Conclusion.}
Substituting the above estimates into \eqref{e:diff.eta.terms} gives
the claimed bound.

nodes.statement: Let alpha_textuplbdle dotalphaleddotalphalealpha_textupubd with ddotalpha-dotalpha le exp(-2^k). Our goal is to upper bound the difference Phi(ddotalpha)-Phi(dotalpha) where Phi is the textup1-textscrsb free energy defined by . To this end, define the function \[ G(x,y) equiv lnbigg( frac1e^x+frac1e^y-frac1e^x+y bigg)\,, \] and note that Phi(alpha)=Phi_1(alpha)+(k-1)Phi_2(alpha) where nonumber Phi_1(alpha) &equiv E ln( frac1exp(Sigma^SPIN+) +frac1exp(Sigma^SPIN-) -frac1exp(Sigma^SPIN++Sigma^SPIN-) ) = E G(Sigma^SPIN+,Sigma^SPIN-)\,,\\ Phi_2(alpha) &equiv -alpha\,Eln bigg( 1- prod_j=1^k eta_jbigg) equiv alpha \, E X'\,. We define tildeSigma^SPINtextpm as in the proof of Lemma~, and decompose (similarly to ) \[ Phi_1(ddotalpha) -Phi_1(dotalpha) =overbraceE bigg( G(ddotSigma^SPIN+,ddotSigma^SPIN-) -G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) bigg)^textupdenote this G +overbraceEbigg( G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) -G(dotSigma^SPIN+,dotSigma^SPIN-) bigg)^textupdenote this g\,. \] We further decompose \[ g = E Bigg( overbracebigg\ G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) -G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,dotSigma^SPIN-) bigg\^textupdenote this g^SPIN- +overbracebigg\ G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,dotSigma^SPIN-) -G(dotSigma^SPIN+,dotSigma^SPIN-) bigg\^textupdenote this g^SPIN+ Bigg)\,. \] It is easily checked that |G_x|le1 and |G_xx|le1, so \[ g^SPIN+ =overbraceBigg\ sum_i=1^dotd^SPIN+ G_xBig(Sigma^SPIN+[i] + dotX^SPIN+_i, dotSigma^SPIN-Big) cdot Big( ddotX^SPIN+_i - dotX^SPIN+_i Big) Bigg\ ^textupdenote this g_x +overbrace OBigg( sum_i=1^dotd^SPIN+ Big( ddotX^SPIN+_i - dotX^SPIN+_i Big)^2Bigg) ^textupdenote this g_xx. \] Applying Corollary~ gives \[ (Eg^SPIN+)^2 le 2\, Ebigg( E[ g_x\,|\,dotT]^2 +E[ g_xx\,|\,dotT]^2 bigg) le frac(ddotalpha-dotalpha)^2 2^3k/k^O(1) + frac(ddotalpha-dotalpha)^2 2^6k/k^O(1) le frac(ddotalpha-dotalpha)^2 2^3k/k^O(1)\,. \] Similar bounds hold for g^SPIN-, so we conclude \[|g| =bigg| EBig(g^SPIN-+g^SPIN-Big) bigg| le fracddotalpha-dotalpha 2^3k/2/k^O(1)\,.\] It remains to estimate G. This is similar to the analysis of A in the proof of Lemma~: write deltaequivddotd-dotd=delta^SPIN++delta^SPIN- for the difference in root degrees between dotT and ddotT. When delta=0 we have simply G=0. The expected contribution from the event deltage2 is negligible. It remains to consider the case delta=1. Without loss of generality, take the case that delta^SPIN+=1 and delta^SPIN-=0: G_1,0 &equivEBigg[ G(ddotSigma^SPIN+,ddotSigma^SPIN-) -G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) ; (delta^SPIN+,delta^SPIN-)=(1,0)Bigg]\\ &=EBigg[ G(tildeSigma^SPIN+ + ddotX_ddotd^SPIN+, tildeSigma^SPIN-) -G(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) ; (delta^SPIN+,delta^SPIN-)=(1,0)Bigg]\\ &= -frac12 cdot frack (ddotalpha-dotalpha)2 cdot frac1+O(2^-k/20) 2^k-1\,, where the last estimate uses Lemma~ and the fact that the partial derivative G_x(tildeSigma^SPIN+,tildeSigma^SPIN-) is well concentrated around -1/2. Altogether we conclude \[Phi_1(ddotalpha) -Phi_1(dotalpha) = - frack(ddotalpha-dotalpha) 2^k Bigg\ 1 + fracO(1)2^k/20 Bigg\\,. \] Next, let dotX' and ddotX' be defined analogously to X' in , but using the messages doteta_j and ddoteta_j. Then \[ Phi_2(ddotalpha)-Phi_2(dotalpha) = overbracebigg\ (ddotalpha-dotalpha) cdot EdotX' bigg\^textupdenote this h_21 + overbracebigg\ ddotalpha\,E(ddotX'-dotX') bigg\^textupdenote this h_22 \,. \] A trivial modification of Corollary~ gives \[ (Eh_22)^2 le fracddotalpha^2 (ddotalpha-dotalpha) 2^5k/k^O(1) lefrac(ddotalpha-dotalpha) 2^3k/k^O(1)\,. \] On the other hand, a trivial modification of bounds from Lemma~ (with k in place of k-1) gives \[Eh_21 = fracddotalpha-dotalpha2^k Bigg\ 1 + fracO(1)2^k/20 Bigg\ \,.\] Combining the above estimates gives finally \[ Phi(ddotalpha) -Phi(dotalpha) =Bigg\ - frack(ddotalpha-dotalpha) 2^k +frac(k-1)(ddotalpha-dotalpha)2^k Bigg\ Bigg\ 1 + fracO(1)2^k/20 Bigg\ = - fracddotalpha-dotalpha 2^k Bigg\ 1 + fracO(k)2^k/20 Bigg\\,. \] This proves that Phi is strictly decreasing on the interval alpha_textuplbdlealphalealpha_textupubd, as desired.
